chapters.title: Chapter 1 Should I Give Her an Injection
paragraphs: Good news: Zhang Shan had transmigrated to another world, and he even brought a Super Rebate System along for the ride.
Bad news: The damn thing was broken.

Before him lay endless, sprawling mountains. The village he was stuck in was so small and insignificant it didn’t even have a name. Every night, Zhang Shan would climb onto the roof and stare blankly at the sky.

"My life is over. Maybe I should just end it here. Take this defective System with me, reroll my save file, and start over." Zhang Shan gazed up at the bright full moon, his suicidal thoughts bubbling to the surface yet again.
In his previous life, he had been a corporate drone who died from overwork. When he first arrived in this new world, he was brimming with confidence and ambition. After all, he had a System.
"With my knowledge of science and the Super Rebate System, I’ll reach the peak of this world within three years!"
Born into poverty in the mountains? No big deal.
Raised by a hunter as a foster father? Not a problem.
Honestly, it was better than transmigrating into a rich family—no need to fear backstabbing relatives or endure the humiliation of a "crippled trash" start.
He had a perfect starting hand. It was a guaranteed win.
But not long after, panic set in.

This village was completely cut off from the outside world. To call it a "godforsaken backwater" would be a compliment. If not for the ancient tombstones carved by past village chiefs on the distant burial mounds, Zhang Shan would have doubted whether he was even in a civilized human society.
And then there was the System he brought with him—it was even worse than the location.
To be fair, the System itself was incredible: once he bonded with a target and gifted them something, he would receive an enormous return. The more he gave, the richer he would become.
But there was one critical condition: only a "Daughter of Destiny"—as defined by the System—could trigger these returns.
Where the hell was he supposed to find a Daughter of Destiny in this forgotten corner of the world?!
Zhang Shan cursed loudly. On his very first day, he had scrutinized every living thing in the village. He even checked the bird eggs in the nests.
Nothing.
"It seems I’ll have to rely on my own strength to leave these mountains," Zhang Shan thought, still nurturing dreams of the big city. He diligently learned farming and hunting from his foster father.
Five years passed.
Zhang Shan found himself constantly longing for his old 996 work schedule. Compared to surviving in the wild, being exploited by capitalists felt like a luxury vacation.
Then, the village chief fell ill and died. Zhang Shan personally carved the tombstone for him.
From that moment on, Zhang Shan became the only literate person left in the village.
Around the same time, he gained a little sidekick—a five-year-old girl with messy black hair whom the village chief had picked up off the streets.
That year, Zhang Shan turned twenty.
"This girl will be your wife someday. Her food and clothing are your responsibility now," his foster father told him.

Looking into the little girl’s pitiful eyes, seeing her covered in dirt and grime, Zhang Shan felt nothing but despair. "I’m destined to leave these mountains and marry a princess! Marrying this dirty little brat? I might as well hang myself."
Ten more years passed.
Zhang Shan still hadn’t managed to escape the mountains. All he had gained were countless scars.
During this time, he personally erected over a dozen tombstones, including one for his hunter foster father.
The memories of the previous generation were slowly fading away, buried under the earth one by one.
As for the System... Ha! What a piece of junk!
[Ding! Daughter of Destiny discovered: Zhang Lele.]
Late at night, a notification chimed in his mind, jolting Zhang Shan awake from his daze on the rooftop.
What the hell?! Who is Zhang Lele?
Zhang Shan thought he was hallucinating, but the ethereal subtitles floating before his eyes confirmed it was real.
Lele... Lele... Oh my god! The black-haired girl!
Zhang Shan nearly did a backflip in surprise. Why the brat? And why now?
His mind was flooded with questions, but none of that mattered. As long as there was a return, the System could declare a dog to be the Daughter of Destiny and he’d accept it happily.
"I’m finally going to get rich!" Zhang Shan wept tears of excitement.
"Hey! Brat! Wake up!" He burst into the room, moving faster than he ever had in his life.
"Ouch..." The girl before him slowly sat up, still half-asleep.
Looking at the girl in front of him, Zhang Shan simply couldn’t reconcile her with the title "Daughter of Destiny."
Her hair was stringy and greasy, her skin rough and flaky—she was utterly unappealing.

This girl was light-years away from the women he’d known in his previous life. Forget smooth, fair skin or a curvaceous figure—she couldn’t even compare to the village’s pretty widow whose husband died a few years back. At least the widow had a nice ass!
"Brother Shan, I just fell asleep. What do you want now?" the girl mumbled. Her eyes were barely open, but she instinctively wrapped her legs around Zhang Shan and snuggled close.
Unlike Zhang Shan, the girl had always considered herself his little wife. She was fifteen now—old enough to bear children for Brother Shan!
[Ding! Zhang Lele’s destiny attribute remains unactivated; bonding failed.]
Zhang Shan was dumbfounded.
He almost spat out a mouthful of blood from sheer frustration.
Me?!
What the...?!
Why the hell?!
His inner self roared with fury. If the System had a physical body, he would have hung it up and beaten it mercilessly for a full year!
You’re messing with me! You’re playing tricks on me! What does "unactivated" even mean?!
How do I activate it? Does touching her work?
Zhang Shan gently touched the girl’s thigh.
She froze, her dark complexion gradually flushing a soft pink.
"Brother Shan, where are you touching? Are you...?"
In her mind, she recalled the raunchy jokes shared among the village women. Just thinking about them made her head spin.
Oh no! This is so embarrassing!
Though a bit scared, she felt far more shy—and eager.
Zhang Shan waited for a long while, but the System remained silent.
Damn it! After cursing the System for thirty thousand words in his head, Zhang Shan launched into a frantic brainstorm.
Could it be that I need to give her an... injection?
No way! She’s too young. What’s the difference between me and a beast if I do that?
At least wait until she’s eighteen—no, sixteen!
"Brother Shan, are you okay?" the girl asked, her big eyes wide.
"I’m fine." Unwilling to give up, Zhang Shan touched her face, pinched her shoulders, squeezed her feet, and even kissed her forehead—but still, no activation.
The girl was both shocked and flustered. Never before had her Brother Shan been so proactive!
Unfortunately, Zhang Shan didn’t follow through, leaving her with a lingering sense of disappointment.
Does he think I haven’t developed enough? But I’m still so young! The girl fumed inwardly.
Zhang Shan spent the entire day racking his brain about the activation method, yet he still had no clue. Finally, evening arrived.
Tonight was the night of the full moon. It was the girl's favorite time because Brother Shan always told her stories on these nights.
"Brother Shan, Brother Shan! If it were you, who would you like better? Xiao Zhao is gentle and pitiful, Zhi Ruo has a tragic fate, and Princess Minmin is bold and passionate—oh, I love them all!"
"Of course I’d want them all!" Zhang Shan clenched his fist, imagining himself as the greedy official from the stories.
"Tch! Brother Shan is such a lecher!" The girl pretended to be angry.
She had been with Zhang Shan for ten years. She knew how much he longed to leave the mountains, but the world outside was too dangerous, and the mountains too vast.
Brother Shan had nearly died in the wilderness several times. Over the years, he seemed to have given up.
Brother Shan was incredibly talented—he could do almost anything, tell countless fascinating stories, and even teach her to read and write.
Under the moonlight, looking at the faint streaks of gray at his temples, the girl suddenly felt a pang of heartache.
Brother Shan was already thirty. In his stories, thirty was the prime of a man's life, the age of ambition.
But she knew that in these mountains, thirty was already past one's prime. He hadn’t managed to leave in fifteen years; it was even more impossible now.
Poor Brother Shan... these mountains have trapped him. He doesn’t belong here.

Though they were exhausted every day and often went hungry, as long as Brother Shan was by her side, she felt happy. That was why she stubbornly named herself Zhang Lele—"Le" for happiness—because she truly felt happy every day.
She also felt a bit insecure. Alas, she wasn’t like the beautiful, fair-skinned heroines in his books.
But she wasn’t jealous. She had Brother Shan. Even if he didn’t love her, she was content just to stay quietly by his side, even as a humble servant.
As Zhang Shan continued his story, he suddenly heard a soft snore.
He looked down. The black-haired girl was curled up in his arms, fast asleep with a gentle smile on her lips, lost in a sweet dream.
Zhang Shan smiled.
Looking at the girl in his arms... truthfully speaking, she wasn’t ugly at all. Big eyes, small face. As for being dark and dirty, who in these mountains wasn’t?

It was too dangerous here—even taking a bath was a luxury. The water sources were infested with ferocious beasts. Giving her a bath once every two weeks was already the height of luxury in this village.
As for her figure... well, she was a bottomless pit. No matter how much she ate, she never seemed to fill out.
Whatever. I'll just wait until she’s an adult.
There weren’t many households in the village anyway. It wouldn’t do to spend his whole life as a virgin—that would be too miserable.
As for activating her destiny attribute, he’d take it one step at a time. It was probably just another trick played by this damn System.
"Girl, I’ll marry you when you turn eighteen," Zhang Shan murmured softly.
"Really?" The girl’s eyes snapped open, wide as copper bells!
[Ding! 60-point Daughter of Destiny discovered: Nan Gong Yao.]

chapters.title: Chapter 2 Something Fell From the Sky
paragraphs: Again?
As the notification chimed in his mind, a shooting star streaked across the starry canvas above, trailing a blazing tail of heavenly fire before plummeting toward the earth.
BOOM!
A deafening crash echoed through the mountains. Relying on his years of experience as a hunter, Zhang Shan instantly pinpointed the impact site: just two li to the west.
"Nangong Yao? Is it really a person falling from the sky?" he mused. "And this time, the System even gave me a Heavenly Fate score... There’s no way I’m not checking this out."
After being tricked by the System for so many years, Zhang Shan remained surprisingly calm.

He made a sharp gesture to silence Xiao Hei. She understood immediately—this wasn’t the time for fooling around. With practiced ease, she flipped off the roof and reappeared moments later, carrying a woven basket on her back, two short daggers tucked at her waist, and clutching the wooden bow Brother Shan was accustomed to using.
Meanwhile, Zhang Shan had geared up, gripping a steel fishing spear in his hand. Together, the two dashed toward the crash site.

In no time at all, they arrived at a stream. The once-familiar landscape had been utterly transformed, the earth scorched and charred black. And there, leaning against a rocky outcrop, lay a slender figure.
The moment Zhang Shan laid eyes on the woman, his heart skipped a beat.

She was young, seemingly no older than twenty, with an exquisite figure and breathtaking beauty. Though her face bore a faint, sickly pallor, she was more stunning than any celebrity Zhang Shan had ever seen in his previous life. Her cascading hair flowed freely in the wind, strands clinging softly to her neck, accentuating her skin’s icy, translucent glow.

Her white robes, scorched by heavenly fire, were tattered and torn, revealing glimpses of alabaster skin marred by several deep, crimson wounds. She stood barefoot, her delicate arches graceful yet stained with dirt and blood.

This ravaged appearance was almost too much for Zhang Shan to bear. A wave of heat surged straight to his crown, nearly overwhelming him. Had he not been mentally prepared, he might have lost all composure right then and there.
[Ding! Nangong Yao’s Favorability toward you is -1. Binding successful.]
Zhang Shan nearly burst into tears on the spot.
Thank goodness he hadn’t rushed to "inoculate" Xiao Hei yesterday! Otherwise, what would he be but a beast?
A living, breathing Heavenly Fate beauty had fallen right into his lap—what a gift from the System!
Xiao Hei, standing beside him, was equally mesmerized. She’d never seen anyone so beautiful in her entire life.

But Zhang Shan quickly regained his vigilance. This exquisite woman had fallen from the sky like a meteor, yet appeared completely intact. A faint, golden aura enveloped her body, radiating a gentle warmth. All signs pointed to her being a cultivator—or even an Immortal.
The cultivation world was notorious for its ruthless nature. One couldn’t afford to be deceived by a dazzling exterior. What if she was a merciless demoness?

The woman had noticed the two wild figures long ago. She hadn’t expected to find mortals in these vast, desolate mountains. But these two posed no threat to her. With a soft exhale, she spoke gently, "Do you happen to have any water or food?"
"Ah... yes, we do!" Xiao Hei was the first to react, scrambling to pull an oil-paper package from her bag.
Zhang Shan didn’t stop her. This woman could crush him as easily as swatting a fly. All he could do was curry favor for now and see how things unfolded.
After nibbling on some wild vegetable cakes and sipping a few mouthfuls of spring water, the woman gradually regained her strength, circulating her Qi through several rounds of the Celestial Circuit.

Her name was Nangong Yao, an Elder of the renowned Yunmiao Sect, one of the most prestigious cultivation factions of the current era. She had ventured into a Secret Realm, only to suffer a catastrophic failure. She had barely managed to escape by burning her blood essence to unleash a life-saving technique.

The loss of a few mouthfuls of essence had cost her decades of cultivation progress, leaving Nangong Yao deeply disheartened. To her, these two individuals were nothing more than mountain savages. If they could communicate, that was fortunate; if they could offer her mundane food, even better—it might help her recover sooner.
But this vegetable cake was truly awful.
"I also have some medicinal herbs here, if you’re interested, my Lady." Zhang Shan glanced at the woman’s bare feet, involuntarily swallowing hard. Those milky-white legs...
[Ding! Nangong Yao’s Favorability toward you decreases by 1. Current Favorability: -2.]
Nangong Yao frowned slightly, drawing her feet closer and suppressing the urge to strike him down with a single sword slash. "No need!" she snapped coldly.

She cast a sidelong glance at the rugged man. His physique suggested he was around thirty, riddled with hidden ailments. His Qi and blood were chaotic, and he was devoid of any Spiritual Roots. He likely didn’t have many years left to live.
Tch, utter trash.
Then her gaze shifted to the somewhat shy Xiao Hei beside him.

Hmm... this girl seems to be around fifteen, with abundant Qi and blood foundations. Wait... she actually possesses Spiritual Roots! Not just any roots—she has an exceptional Water Spirit Root! No, wait—there is also a trace of a Gold Spirit Root!

Nangong Yao occupied a high position and had encountered countless talented youths, but she had never met anyone as gifted as Xiao Hei. Even she found herself unable to fully fathom the girl’s potential.

If I could bring this girl into the sect, the rewards I’d receive might surpass everything I’ve gained from years of exploring Secret Realms combined! Nangong Yao felt a surge of excitement deep within her.
"Ahem... Little girl, what is your name?"
The fairy’s voice was as enchanting as her appearance. Xiao Hei was momentarily dazed. "M-me... my name is Zhang Lele."
"Miss Lele, I will trouble you to bring me some food and fresh water over the next few days. I promise a generous reward afterward," Nangong Yao said, trying her best to sound gentle.
Xiao Hei turned to Zhang Shan with a questioning look. The Fairy Sister was so beautiful; she felt terribly inadequate standing next to her.
"The Fairy can stay temporarily at my place with Lele—we—" Zhang Shan interjected.
"No need for that! Just Miss Lele will do."
[Ding! Nangong Yao’s Favorability toward you decreases by 1. Current Favorability: -3.]
Damn it! This woman is far too arrogant! Zhang Shan seethed inwardly.
For the next half month, Nangong Yao rested by the riverside.

Zhang Shan went all out, even resorting to extreme measures. He slaughtered a mountain chicken to prepare a lavish lunch for Nangong Yao every day—a feast rivaling the grandest holiday meals. He even went to the riverbank to shave his beard and scrubbed his tattered clothes until they shone anew.
To finally bind a Daughter of Destiny, only to find himself unable to even approach her—it was ten thousand times worse than an aging eunuch visiting a brothel.
Zhang Shan was desperate—desperately so!
But his efforts weren’t entirely in vain. Over the course of half a month, he appeared before Nangong Yao five times, and her Favorability steadily dropped to -8 points.
Xiao Hei’s mood had also been rather sour these past few days. The Fairy Sister was beautiful and unpretentious, but she treated Brother Shan with such coldness.
The brother she’d admired for over ten years was now shamelessly fawning over the Fairy Sister, even offering her the finest cuts of meat! Humph! So angry!
And to make matters worse, the Fairy Sister treated Brother Shan with such icy indifference! Even angrier!!
Finally, one evening, Nangong Yao had fully recovered her strength.
It was time to return to the sect, and she decided to take Xiao Hei along.

Nangong Yao raised her hand and performed a magical incantation. A shimmering curtain of water appeared before her. She stepped lightly into the curtain, and when she emerged again, she found herself standing at the doorstep of Zhang Shan's small thatched cottage.

At that very moment, Zhang Shan was sitting outside, bandaging his wounds. These past few days, he’d been preparing rich meat dishes for Nangong Yao daily, sustaining minor injuries from intense hunting expeditions. Xiao Hei sat beside him, pouting as she ground up a clump of dark, smelly herbs.
When Nangong Yao suddenly appeared before them, both Zhang Shan and Xiao Hei sprang to their feet.

"Thank you for your kindness these past few days. I have recovered almost completely and plan to depart today. Miss Lele, I sense you possess remarkable talent. I intend to take you back to the sect for cultivation," Nangong Yao announced calmly, yet with an unmistakable tone that brooked no refusal.
"And what about Brother Shan?"
"He is merely an ordinary mortal, incapable of cultivation. Miss Lele, your talent is extraordinary; your future accomplishments will surely surpass even mine."
Xiao Hei felt a sudden wave of tension and instinctively reached out to grasp Zhang Shan’s arm.
This scene displeased Nangong Yao greatly. Over the past few days, she had occasionally extended her Spiritual Awareness to Xiao Hei, discovering just how deeply dependent the girl was on Zhang Shan.

Zhang Shan’s nature wasn’t entirely bad, but Nangong Yao could clearly perceive his underhanded intentions. Still, none of that mattered. His Qi and blood were chaotic, making him utterly unfit to refine spiritual energy. He was destined to remain unqualified for cultivation forever.

Xiao Hei took several deep breaths, then looked directly at Nangong Yao and said, "I—I can go with you for cultivation, but I have one condition: Brother Shan must come with us, even if he can’t cultivate."

These words had been taught to her by Zhang Shan. She had no idea why he thought the Fairy Sister would take her for cultivation, but it turned out exactly as he’d predicted—Brother Shan was truly remarkable!
What a joke! A Daughter of Destiny recognized by the System! Of course Nangong Yao knows talent when she sees it.

Zhang Shan rejoiced inwardly. Over these past few days, he had envisioned countless scenarios and possibilities, for this was his only chance to leave the mountains. Besides, how could Xiao Hei, a Daughter of Destiny, truly spend her entire life cooped up in this wilderness?

Nangong Yao frowned slightly. This girl was incredibly gifted, yet utterly inexperienced and naive. Moreover, her particular lineage of cultivation was quite unique—how could she possibly remain entangled with an ordinary mortal?
"No."
"Then I won’t go either!" Xiao Hei pouted again.
"You—" Nangong Yao flared up in anger. Here was an opportunity that tens of thousands applied for each year, yet this girl showed no appreciation for it.

Perhaps it would be simpler to just knock her unconscious and take her away! After all, once she experienced the splendor of the cultivation world, along with the other handsome and talented male disciples in the sect, she’d likely forget this mountain pig of a mortal in no time.
Seeing the awkward atmosphere, Zhang Shan suggested, "Why don’t you let Lele go with you for cultivation, and simply take me to the nearest city?"
He reasoned that once they were out of these mountains, anything could be negotiated.

Nangong Yao shook her head. "My sect resides far above the Celestial Threshold. Your chaotic Qi and blood wouldn’t survive even ten breaths there. Besides, within a thousand li radius, there isn’t a single city—this place is even more dangerous than these mountains."

Seeing that Xiao Hei remained silent, Nangong Yao sighed softly. Zhang Lele’s talent was too extraordinary; her future achievements would undoubtedly be significant. She didn’t want to force the issue, lest she incur the girl’s resentment later.

So she continued, "How about this: Miss Lele, you come with me back to the sect. Within two years, I guarantee you will achieve Foundation Establishment. At that time, you can return whenever you wish. In addition, I will grant him a life of worldly wealth and prosperity."
"No!" Xiao Hei stubbornly refused.
Just knock her unconscious already! Nangong Yao was furious.

sentences.text: Again?
As the notification chimed in his mind, a shooting star streaked across the starry canvas above, trailing a blazing tail of heavenly fire before plummeting toward the earth.
BOOM!
A deafening crash echoed through the mountains.
Relying on his years of experience as a hunter, Zhang Shan instantly pinpointed the impact site: just two li to the west.
"Nangong Yao?
Is it really a person falling from the sky?" he mused.
"And this time, the System even gave me a Heavenly Fate score...
There’s no way I’m not checking this out."
After being tricked by the System for so many years, Zhang Shan remained surprisingly calm.
He made a sharp gesture to silence Xiao Hei.
She understood immediately—this wasn’t the time for fooling around.

With practiced ease, she flipped off the roof and reappeared moments later, carrying a woven basket on her back, two short daggers tucked at her waist, and clutching the wooden bow Brother Shan was accustomed to using.
Meanwhile, Zhang Shan had geared up, gripping a steel fishing spear in his hand.
Together, the two dashed toward the crash site.
In no time at all, they arrived at a stream.
The once-familiar landscape had been utterly transformed, the earth scorched and charred black.
And there, leaning against a rocky outcrop, lay a slender figure.
The moment Zhang Shan laid eyes on the woman, his heart skipped a beat.
She was young, seemingly no older than twenty, with an exquisite figure and breathtaking beauty.
Though her face bore a faint, sickly pallor, she was more stunning than any celebrity Zhang Shan had ever seen in his previous life.
Her cascading hair flowed freely in the wind, strands clinging softly to her neck, accentuating her skin’s icy, translucent glow.
Her white robes, scorched by heavenly fire, were tattered and torn, revealing glimpses of alabaster skin marred by several deep, crimson wounds.
She stood barefoot, her delicate arches graceful yet stained with dirt and blood.
This ravaged appearance was almost too much for Zhang Shan to bear.
A wave of heat surged straight to his crown, nearly overwhelming him.
Had he not been mentally prepared, he might have lost all composure right then and there.
[Ding!
Nangong Yao’s Favorability toward you is -1.
Binding successful.]
Zhang Shan nearly burst into tears on the spot.
Thank goodness he hadn’t rushed to "inoculate" Xiao Hei yesterday!
Otherwise, what would he be but a beast?
A living, breathing Heavenly Fate beauty had fallen right into his lap—what a gift from the System!
Xiao Hei, standing beside him, was equally mesmerized.
She’d never seen anyone so beautiful in her entire life.
But Zhang Shan quickly regained his vigilance.
This exquisite woman had fallen from the sky like a meteor, yet appeared completely intact.
A faint, golden aura enveloped her body, radiating a gentle warmth.
All signs pointed to her being a cultivator—or even an Immortal.
The cultivation world was notorious for its ruthless nature.
One couldn’t afford to be deceived by a dazzling exterior.
What if she was a merciless demoness?
The woman had noticed the two wild figures long ago.
She hadn’t expected to find mortals in these vast, desolate mountains.
But these two posed no threat to her.
With a soft exhale, she spoke gently, "Do you happen to have any water or food?"
"Ah... yes, we do!" Xiao Hei was the first to react, scrambling to pull an oil-paper package from her bag.
Zhang Shan didn’t stop her.
This woman could crush him as easily as swatting a fly.
All he could do was curry favor for now and see how things unfolded.
After nibbling on some wild vegetable cakes and sipping a few mouthfuls of spring water, the woman gradually regained her strength, circulating her Qi through several rounds of the Celestial Circuit.
Her name was Nangong Yao, an Elder of the renowned Yunmiao Sect, one of the most prestigious cultivation factions of the current era.
She had ventured into a Secret Realm, only to suffer a catastrophic failure.
She had barely managed to escape by burning her blood essence to unleash a life-saving technique.
The loss of a few mouthfuls of essence had cost her decades of cultivation progress, leaving Nangong Yao deeply disheartened.
To her, these two individuals were nothing more than mountain savages.
If they could communicate, that was fortunate; if they could offer her mundane food, even better—it might help her recover sooner.
But this vegetable cake was truly awful.
"I also have some medicinal herbs here, if you’re interested, my Lady." Zhang Shan glanced at the woman’s bare feet, involuntarily swallowing hard.
Those milky-white legs...
[Ding!
Nangong Yao’s Favorability toward you decreases by 1.
Current Favorability: -2.]
Nangong Yao frowned slightly, drawing her feet closer and suppressing the urge to strike him down with a single sword slash.
"No need!" she snapped coldly.
She cast a sidelong glance at the rugged man.
His physique suggested he was around thirty, riddled with hidden ailments.
His Qi and blood were chaotic, and he was devoid of any Spiritual Roots.
He likely didn’t have many years left to live.
Tch, utter trash.
Then her gaze shifted to the somewhat shy Xiao Hei beside him.
Hmm... this girl seems to be around fifteen, with abundant Qi and blood foundations.
Wait... she actually possesses Spiritual Roots!
Not just any roots—she has an exceptional Water Spirit Root!
No, wait—there is also a trace of a Gold Spirit Root!
Nangong Yao occupied a high position and had encountered countless talented youths, but she had never met anyone as gifted as Xiao Hei.
Even she found herself unable to fully fathom the girl’s potential.
If I could bring this girl into the sect, the rewards I’d receive might surpass everything I’ve gained from years of exploring Secret Realms combined!
Nangong Yao felt a surge of excitement deep within her.
"Ahem...
Little girl, what is your name?"
The fairy’s voice was as enchanting as her appearance.
Xiao Hei was momentarily dazed.
"M-me... my name is Zhang Lele."
"Miss Lele, I will trouble you to bring me some food and fresh water over the next few days.
I promise a generous reward afterward," Nangong Yao said, trying her best to sound gentle.
Xiao Hei turned to Zhang Shan with a questioning look.
The Fairy Sister was so beautiful; she felt terribly inadequate standing next to her.
"The Fairy can stay temporarily at my place with Lele—we—" Zhang Shan interjected.
"No need for that!
Just Miss Lele will do."
[Ding!
Nangong Yao’s Favorability toward you decreases by 1.
Current Favorability: -3.]
Damn it!
This woman is far too arrogant!
Zhang Shan seethed inwardly.
For the next half month, Nangong Yao rested by the riverside.
Zhang Shan went all out, even resorting to extreme measures.
He slaughtered a mountain chicken to prepare a lavish lunch for Nangong Yao every day—a feast rivaling the grandest holiday meals.
He even went to the riverbank to shave his beard and scrubbed his tattered clothes until they shone anew.
To finally bind a Daughter of Destiny, only to find himself unable to even approach her—it was ten thousand times worse than an aging eunuch visiting a brothel.
Zhang Shan was desperate—desperately so!
But his efforts weren’t entirely in vain.
Over the course of half a month, he appeared before Nangong Yao five times, and her Favorability steadily dropped to -8 points.
Xiao Hei’s mood had also been rather sour these past few days.
The Fairy Sister was beautiful and unpretentious, but she treated Brother Shan with such coldness.
The brother she’d admired for over ten years was now shamelessly fawning over the Fairy Sister, even offering her the finest cuts of meat!
Humph!
So angry!
And to make matters worse, the Fairy Sister treated Brother Shan with such icy indifference!
Even angrier!!
Finally, one evening, Nangong Yao had fully recovered her strength.
It was time to return to the sect, and she decided to take Xiao Hei along.
Nangong Yao raised her hand and performed a magical incantation.
A shimmering curtain of water appeared before her.
She stepped lightly into the curtain, and when she emerged again, she found herself standing at the doorstep of Zhang Shan's small thatched cottage.
At that very moment, Zhang Shan was sitting outside, bandaging his wounds.
These past few days, he’d been preparing rich meat dishes for Nangong Yao daily, sustaining minor injuries from intense hunting expeditions.
Xiao Hei sat beside him, pouting as she ground up a clump of dark, smelly herbs.
When Nangong Yao suddenly appeared before them, both Zhang Shan and Xiao Hei sprang to their feet.
"Thank you for your kindness these past few days.
I have recovered almost completely and plan to depart today.
Miss Lele, I sense you possess remarkable talent.
I intend to take you back to the sect for cultivation," Nangong Yao announced calmly, yet with an unmistakable tone that brooked no refusal.
"And what about Brother Shan?"
"He is merely an ordinary mortal, incapable of cultivation.
Miss Lele, your talent is extraordinary; your future accomplishments will surely surpass even mine."
Xiao Hei felt a sudden wave of tension and instinctively reached out to grasp Zhang Shan’s arm.
This scene displeased Nangong Yao greatly.
Over the past few days, she had occasionally extended her Spiritual Awareness to Xiao Hei, discovering just how deeply dependent the girl was on Zhang Shan.
Zhang Shan’s nature wasn’t entirely bad, but Nangong Yao could clearly perceive his underhanded intentions.
Still, none of that mattered.
His Qi and blood were chaotic, making him utterly unfit to refine spiritual energy.
He was destined to remain unqualified for cultivation forever.

Xiao Hei took several deep breaths, then looked directly at Nangong Yao and said, "I—I can go with you for cultivation, but I have one condition: Brother Shan must come with us, even if he can’t cultivate."
These words had been taught to her by Zhang Shan.
She had no idea why he thought the Fairy Sister would take her for cultivation, but it turned out exactly as he’d predicted—Brother Shan was truly remarkable!
What a joke!
A Daughter of Destiny recognized by the System!
Of course Nangong Yao knows talent when she sees it.
Zhang Shan rejoiced inwardly.
Over these past few days, he had envisioned countless scenarios and possibilities, for this was his only chance to leave the mountains.
Besides, how could Xiao Hei, a Daughter of Destiny, truly spend her entire life cooped up in this wilderness?
Nangong Yao frowned slightly.
This girl was incredibly gifted, yet utterly inexperienced and naive.
Moreover, her particular lineage of cultivation was quite unique—how could she possibly remain entangled with an ordinary mortal?
"No."
"Then I won’t go either!" Xiao Hei pouted again.
"You—" Nangong Yao flared up in anger.
Here was an opportunity that tens of thousands applied for each year, yet this girl showed no appreciation for it.
Perhaps it would be simpler to just knock her unconscious and take her away!

After all, once she experienced the splendor of the cultivation world, along with the other handsome and talented male disciples in the sect, she’d likely forget this mountain pig of a mortal in no time.
Seeing the awkward atmosphere, Zhang Shan suggested, "Why don’t you let Lele go with you for cultivation, and simply take me to the nearest city?"
He reasoned that once they were out of these mountains, anything could be negotiated.
Nangong Yao shook her head.
"My sect resides far above the Celestial Threshold.
Your chaotic Qi and blood wouldn’t survive even ten breaths there.
Besides, within a thousand li radius, there isn’t a single city—this place is even more dangerous than these mountains."
Seeing that Xiao Hei remained silent, Nangong Yao sighed softly.
Zhang Lele’s talent was too extraordinary; her future achievements would undoubtedly be significant.
She didn’t want to force the issue, lest she incur the girl’s resentment later.
So she continued, "How about this: Miss Lele, you come with me back to the sect.
Within two years, I guarantee you will achieve Foundation Establishment.
At that time, you can return whenever you wish.
In addition, I will grant him a life of worldly wealth and prosperity."
"No!" Xiao Hei stubbornly refused.
Just knock her unconscious already!
Nangong Yao was furious.

chapters.title: Chapter 3 A Hundred Times Worse Than a Nightmare
paragraphs: Zhang Shan knew he was about to infuriate Nan Gong Yao if he kept pushing, so he pivoted quickly.

"Lele, be good now. Think about it—if all else fails, you can learn some skills and come back to rescue me, right? By then, you’ll be just as powerful as the Fairy, flying through the skies and tunneling through the earth. I’ll be relying on you for support! It’s only a few short years. Don’t worry; the Fairy Sister will soon reward us with plenty of wonderful things, and we’ll finally have someone influential to lean on!"
Who said I’d reward you with wonderful things?! And how could there be "plenty"?
Nan Gong Yao clenched her silver teeth. How could this boar-like savage be so shameless?

Still, she forced herself to cooperate. "Very well. This is a talisman from my sect, imbued with my spiritual energy. Once you wear it, ordinary demonic beasts won’t be able to harm you, ensuring your safety for a lifetime."

With a flick of her delicate hand, a jade token flew straight to Zhang Shan. He caught it—a palm-sized piece of pale-green jade, embroidered with the character "Yao." It felt warm and smooth to the touch, instantly washing him with a sense of calm.
"A treasure!" Zhang Shan quickly tucked it into his robes.

Seeing that Zhang Shan had already accepted the payout, the little dark-haired girl realized she’d been completely sold out. Besides, she wasn’t stupid. Who wouldn’t dream of flying through the skies? And the thought of being able to support Brother Shan in the future filled her heart with sweetness. Still, the idea of being separated from him for several years left her deeply reluctant.
"Thank you, Fairy Sister! But even if I can’t cultivate, would you mind teaching me a few techniques for ordinary people? At least something to strengthen my body and improve my health."

Zhang Shan wasn’t satisfied with just the jade token. Someone had merely offered him a sip of soup, and it had already benefited him immensely. What did a little shame matter? He had to grab as much as he could!
Shameless! He is actually pushing his luck even further!
Nan Gong Yao’s ample chest rose and fell with indignation. If not for the little girl’s expectant gaze, she would have blasted him with a bolt of heavenly thunder right then and there.
Taking a deep breath, Nan Gong Yao conjured a small book and tossed it onto the table. "This manual of Primordial Martial Arts from the mortal realm should be enough for you."
Holy shit, this is incredible!

Zhang Shan eagerly grabbed it. The cover read "Primordial Five Energies," the characters elegant and refined. He flipped through it casually, finding it richly illustrated with both text and images. Another treasure! A secret manual personally written by the Fairy, still carrying a faint, delicate fragrance.
Zhang Shan tucked it into his chest right next to the jade.
Meanwhile, Zhang Shan spent a long while coaxing the little dark-haired girl, who cried uncontrollably, smearing snot and tears all over him.
Finally, Zhang Shan urged the girl toward Nan Gong Yao.
"Let’s go," Nan Gong Yao urged quickly, unable to bear staying a moment longer.

"Fairy Sister, please wait!" Zhang Shan suddenly shouted, pulling a short dagger from his belt and offering it forward with both hands. "Fairy Sister, this short dagger is my gift to you, in gratitude for bestowing upon me such treasures and for helping Lele cultivate her skills."
What is he doing?
It felt as if a dog had suddenly decided to share its most treasured bone with her. Nan Gong Yao was taken aback.

Zhang Shan scrambled to explain, "I know the Fairy Sister has no use for such mundane items, but you’ve shown great kindness toward us. This dagger is a custom passed down through generations in our village. If you don’t accept it, both Lele and I will feel guilty and ashamed before our ancestors."
"Exactly! That’s right!" the little dark-haired girl chimed in.
Seeing that Zhang Shan had even invoked his ancestors, Nan Gong Yao was speechless. Fine, fine—I’ll just swallow my pride!
With a flick of her sleeve, the short dagger vanished. "I accept your gift. Let’s go."
[Ding! First-time gift of a "Defective Short Dagger" successful.] [Triggered Return: Low-grade magical artifact, the Ruyi Short Sword.]

[Special Reminder: The gifted item must be something the Daughter of Destiny needs to trigger a return. However, as this is the Host’s first gift, the return was successful. This exception will not be repeated.]
[Ruyi Short Sword: Low-grade magical artifact. Moves at the heart’s command, capable of striking enemies from a thousand zhang away.]
[Ding! Congratulations, Host! Your first gift triggered the Newcomer Gift: Space Treasury and the Ninefold Nirvana Pill.]
[Space Treasury: Divine-grade spatial magical artifact. Like a mustard seed containing Mount Sumeru, capable of storing countless items.]
[Ninefold Nirvana Pill: Divine-grade medicinal pill. After consumption, it strengthens one’s vital essence and blood, and allows one resurrection upon death.]
Zhang Shan felt the expanded space provided by the System and was immediately overwhelmed with joy. So many years of waiting—it hadn’t been easy!
With this Ruyi Short Sword, hunting would never be a worry again. And this divine-grade pill was practically an extra life!
If he could, he would have hugged Nan Gong Yao’s leg and cried his eyes out.
"I’m sorry, System Father! All these years, I misunderstood you!"
"Brother Shan, wait for me for two years... No, no, not even two years—half a year! I’ll come back to see you!" the little dark-haired girl sobbed, already on the verge of tears again.
Nan Gong Yao flipped her hand, and a blanket of light appeared beneath their feet.

"Fairy Sister, couldn’t you take a few wild vegetable cakes too? They’re our village’s specialty! You can’t find them anywhere else!" Zhang Shan tried to squeeze out one last drop of profit, turning to the stove to grab the pot.
Hearing this, Nan Gong Yao quickly made a "shh" sound and whisked the little dark-haired girl away, disappearing into the sky in an instant.
Five years later.

The small village now boasted a two-story building. Zhang Shan looked almost unchanged from five years ago. After consuming the Ninefold Nirvana Pill, his vital essence and blood had strengthened immensely, and his lingering ailments had vanished completely.

The "Primordial Five Energies" was truly an extraordinary martial art. With a single punch, he could split mountains and shatter rocks. Even a bear over two zhang tall could be sent flying by his internal energy alone. If this were a Wuxia world, he would surely be a Grandmaster by now.
Breaking through this mountain range and venturing out shouldn't be too difficult now, Zhang Shan mused.

But the little dark-haired girl remained completely silent. She had promised to return after two years of Foundation Establishment cultivation, yet there was no sign of her. Had something happened? Or did she simply no longer wish to return?
This question lingered in Zhang Shan’s heart. Finally, one day, he decided he couldn’t wait any longer. He had stayed here for twenty whole years. It was time to explore the outside world.
Having prepared everything, Zhang Shan set off.

He remembered Nan Gong Yao and the girl flying northeast, so he headed in that direction. When hungry, he hunted; when thirsty, he drank from streams. The sky was his blanket, the earth his bed, and the stars his guide.

After just half a month, Zhang Shan had traveled thousands of li. Having reached the Primordial Realm, he possessed a sharp sensitivity to danger. He carefully skirted areas where he sensed powerful presences lurking in the mountains.
Since this world had cultivators, it made sense that it also had demons and monsters.

Zhang Shan knew he was vastly stronger than he had been five years ago, but he remained cautious. There was always someone stronger. Take Nan Gong Yao—a top-tier powerhouse. To her, a Primordial-level martial artist like him was insignificant.
Late one night, Zhang Shan suddenly felt a burning sensation in his chest. He pulled out the jade token he’d kept close to his body. It was glowing and warm, though he had no idea what it meant.
Suddenly, a stunning figure in white robes appeared before him—none other than Nan Gong Yao herself.
Zhang Shan was dumbfounded. The goddess from his dreams had materialized right before his eyes.
Is she here to take me to see Lele?
Before he could ask, Nan Gong Yao stared at him with a cold expression and formed a hand seal.
Instantly, Zhang Shan’s heart seized! An unprecedented terror gripped his soul, leaving him no time to react. A blinding golden light flashed before his eyes—
BOOM!
[Ding! Host has died. Consuming the Ninefold Nirvana Pill. Resurrection initiated.]
When Zhang Shan came to, it was already daytime. He lay naked on the grass, his body wracked with excruciating pain.
Did I just die?
Killed by Nan Gong Yao?
Zhang Shan was completely dazed. The sensation of death had been so real, so terrifying—the bone-chilling cold, the instant obliteration of consciousness—that he dared not dwell on it.
Damn it! A divine-grade pill gifted by the System, gone after less than one chapter! Zhang Shan’s heart broke with grief.
Why did she kill me?
As he recalled her cold, serene face and graceful figure, Zhang Shan burst into curses.
"You bitch! I’ll torture you to death! A hundred times worse than a nightmare!"

Why did she kill me?
As he recalled her cold, serene face and graceful figure, Zhang Shan burst into curses.
"You bitch!
I’ll torture you to death!
A hundred times worse than a nightmare!"

chapters.title: Chapter 4 Just Turned Eighteen
paragraphs: Zhang Shan gnashed his teeth, the phantom sensation of death still lingering in his nerves. Rebirth through the Ninefold Nirvana Pill felt as though every bone had been pulverized and reassembled, his soul torn apart by an agony that nearly drove him mad.
She actually came all the way back just to kill me?
But why wait five years to do it?

He forced himself to calm down. Fortunately, the Ruyi Short Sword stored in the System’s Space Treasury was intact. However, all his physical belongings—his clothes, his tools—had been reduced to ash in that golden explosion.
There was no going back to the small village. Suppressing the inferno of rage in his heart, Zhang Shan decided to leave the mountains first. Thoughts of revenge would have to wait.
Three months later.
Zhang Shan stood atop a mountain peak, overlooking a sprawling city laid out like a chessboard on the distant plains.

This was the largest settlement he had seen since leaving the village. The city walls stood ten zhang high, their grayish-blue bricks gleaming coldly in the sunlight. At the gates, a river of carriages and pedestrians flowed endlessly.

At this moment, Zhang Shan was dressed in simple rough-spun cloth, looking every bit the ordinary middle-aged farmer. He had bartered for the clothes at a farmhouse after exiting the wilderness. After asking around, he finally understood where he was.
Daliang.

This kingdom had stood for over five hundred years. Behind him stretched ten thousand li of the Southern Wilderness, a place almost entirely uninhabited by men. As for the "Yunmiao Sect," no one here had ever heard of it. Along his journey, he had heard countless folktales of ghosts and deities, but he hadn't encountered a single genuine cultivator.
The city before him was Yongcheng, the capital of Daliang.

Passing through the towering city gates, the bustling roar of the marketplace surged toward him like a physical tide. Shops lined the streets, vendors shouted their wares incessantly, and pedestrians jostled shoulder to shoulder. Zhang Shan took a deep breath, inhaling the dust and vitality of the mortal world—so utterly different from the silence of the mountains.
He needed a livelihood. And he needed time to process the trauma of that explosion. The sensation of death had given him a profound, new understanding of life.
Two days later.
A notice was posted at the entrance of a courier agency in the western district: "Seeking Couriers. Exceptional martial skills required. Monthly salary starting at five taels."

Zhang Shan stood unremarkably in the line of applicants. Ahead of him was a burly man, broad-shouldered and radiating aggression. Seeing Zhang Shan’s weathered, farmer-like appearance, the man sneered over his shoulder.
"Old man, this isn't rice gruel you're lining up for. This line of work eats people alive—careful you don't lose your old life trying to earn a few coins."
Zhang Shan ignored him completely.
When it was Zhang Shan’s turn, the examiner was a man in his fifties, sitting casually with a fierce scar running down his right cheek.
"What martial arts have you practiced?" the examiner asked.
"Just some self-taught boxing and kicking," Zhang Shan replied plainly.
The examiner frowned. "The Bawang Courier Agency doesn't hire just anyone."
Zhang Shan smiled. "Why don't we spar a little?"
From a distance, he had already assessed that this scarred old man was the strongest fighter in the agency—a Postnatal Realm expert.
No sooner had he spoken than the burly man who had mocked him earlier erupted in anger. "Old man! How dare you challenge Master Ge? You have a death wish!"

Master Ge, seated before them, was one of Daliang’s most renowned experts. The burly man had idolized him since childhood. He had just sparred with Master Ge’s top disciple, lasting a full twenty breaths to pass the interview. Immersed in his triumph, how could he tolerate this dirt-legged farmer disrespecting his hero?
"I'll teach you a lesson!" The burly man lunged.

But before he could even display his technique, his vision blurred. He found himself sailing through the air, propelled by an unseen force, before landing smoothly and safely outside the examination hall.
What just happened?
Confused and dazed, the burly man squeezed his way back into the venue, only to find Master Ge standing solemnly. The scarred master bowed deeply to the farmer, his hands clasped in utmost respect.
"I am Ge Changqing, Chief Courier of the Bawang Courier Agency. May I ask this Senior's honorable name?"
having made a name for himself over many years, Master Ge had eyes sharp as eagles. He recognized the effortless mastery immediately. This farmer was a legendary Primordial Expert!

As soon as Master Ge spoke, the entire venue erupted in astonishment. Master Ge himself was a peak-level Postnatal expert; anyone he called "Senior" could only be a Primordial legend. In all of Daliang, there were fewer than ten recognized Primordial experts, each a figure of immense stature.
Zhang Shan, delighted by the successful display of dominance, returned the bow with a light, carefree gesture.
"Zhang Xian."

He had come seeking the path of cultivation, concealing his true self to walk among mortals. From an ordinary man, he would seek the celestial. Henceforth, he would be known as Zhang Xian—the Immortal Zhang.
And so, Zhang Xian became the Deputy Chief Courier of the Bawang Courier Agency, earning five hundred taels a month.
Spring turned to autumn. Thirty years passed in the blink of an eye.
Zhang Xian became a titan in the capital of Daliang.
In the first ten years, he escorted merchant caravans, protected secret deliveries, and transported tribute for the Royal Family—never failing a single mission.

His most legendary feat was his solo battle against the "Seven Wolves of the Northern Desert." Seven long-renowned experts lasted fewer than ten moves against him combined. The Wolf King, a Primordial expert in his own right, was dispatched by Zhang Xian as easily as one would swat a common fish.

That battle cemented his status in the martial world. It also captured the heart of the Sword Saint’s only daughter. She had been a star since the age of ten, the goddess of Daliang’s martial community, and the dream lover of countless young heroes.
Yet, Zhang Xian plucked the flower.
When their wedding was held, countless knights of Daliang wept and drank themselves into oblivion.
She was eighteen. Zhang Xian was fifty.

In the second decade, Zhang Xian rarely showed his martial hand. The people of Daliang discovered that he was not only a warrior but a literary genius, composing poetry and prose with effortless grace.

His poem, "A single encounter under the golden breeze and jade dew surpasses countless moments in the mortal world," captivated the hearts of the capital's most famous courtesans—a pair of twin sisters. They were coveted by scholars and literati across the land, only to be claimed by the old rogue Zhang Xian.
When their wedding was held, countless talented scholars of Daliang wept and drank themselves into oblivion.
They were eighteen. Zhang Xian was sixty.
In the third decade, Daliang was engulfed in civil strife.

The Third Prince colluded with the Imperial Guard to rebel, besieging the Imperial City. Zhang Xian, accompanied by his disciples, assisted in the defense. He stood alone atop the city walls, holding off the rebel tide. Arrows could not approach him; blades could not wound him. He fully demonstrated the terrifying power of a Perfected Primordial cultivator.

After the rebellion was quelled, the Emperor insisted on a political marriage to bind this powerhouse to the throne. Zhang Xian "reluctantly" accepted, marrying the Emperor’s youngest daughter and receiving the title of Duke Protecting the Nation.

Marrying a princess and being ennobled as a Duke was unprecedented in Daliang’s history. The Little Princess was breathtakingly beautiful, gentle, and adorable—yet another prize claimed by Zhang Xian.
When the news spread, countless nobles and aristocrats who had secretly loved the Little Princess spat blood on the spot.
Zhang Xian, you old bastard! A Grandmaster of martial arts, an old man of seventy, shamelessly pursuing a young beauty—do you have no shame at all?!

When their wedding was held, the entire nation of Daliang drank themselves into oblivion. This time, no one dared to weep openly. The old rogue’s power was simply too overwhelming, and the Imperial Guard was arresting dissenters everywhere.
She was eighteen. Zhang Xian was seventy.

chapters.title: Chapter 5 Youthful Beauty and Silver Hair, But an Instant in Time
paragraphs: Zhang Xian stood atop the mountain peak, gazing at the setting sun in the distance. The wisps of white hair at his temples remained unchanged from years ago, and his face bore no trace of aging.
Youthful beauty and silver hair—mere moments in time.

The once-mighty Bawang Escort Agency had long since changed hands. The Sword Saint’s daughter, the two enchanting twin courtesans, even the Little Princess of the Great Liang Kingdom—all had turned to dust. Yet he alone endured, still alive.

His cultivation in the Innate Realm, coupled with the effects of the Ninefold Nirvana Pill, had arrested his aging. But it had also left him utterly isolated, tasting the true bitterness of loneliness in this world.

Fifty years ago, he had already reached the peak of the Innate Realm. Ten years after that, he had begun to sense the threshold of the next stage. It felt as if a path to true cultivation lay before him, yet it was shrouded in mist, leaving him unable to advance a single step for decades.

Zhang Xian knew this was exactly what Nangong Yao had described: he lacked a Spiritual Root, making cultivation impossible. Even though he had perfected all five elements within himself, he could not generate even a trace of spiritual energy.

Yet these decades had been rich enough in their own right. He had attained the pinnacle of worldly wealth, power, and cherished companions. If he had wished, even the Imperial Throne would have been within his grasp. But after burying his last wife with his own hands, he had nothing left to hold him here. And now, his lifespan was drawing to its end.
With the Innate Realm perfected and the Ninefold Nirvana Pill prolonging his life, he could theoretically live to one hundred fifty.
But now, he was already one hundred twenty.
If this were not a world of cultivation, these years would surely have made for an utterly invincible and exhilarating tale.
Alas...

He had traveled throughout the Great Liang Kingdom, yet never once encountered a cultivator. The System offered no further guidance, and the Yunmiao Sect seemed but a distant dream. Were Nangong Yao and the little black-haired girl still alive? Did Lele still remember him?

Over the years, he had collected countless cultivation manuals. Most were martial arts from the mortal realm—far inferior to the "Innate Five Elements" manual casually gifted to him by Nangong Yao. Occasionally, there were fragments of genuine cultivation texts, but they were either incomplete or belonged to unorthodox sects.

The only text that truly intrigued Zhang Xian was a manual called "Condensing the Golden Core Technique." It was purportedly written by an ancient cultivator who sought to use rare celestial and earthly treasures to condense a false core within the body. This false core would then absorb and refine the spiritual energy of heaven and earth, enabling cultivation. With success, one could reach the Qi Refining or Foundation Establishment stages, and later use that strength to nourish the false core, transforming it into a true Golden Core.

Upon reading it, Zhang Xian was immediately captivated by the author’s vision. Yet regrettably, this "Condensing the Golden Core Technique" remained merely a concept, with many of its processes still crude and theoretical. Despite years of study, Zhang Xian had made no significant breakthroughs.
One day, he wandered to a secluded Taoist temple nestled deep in the mountains.
[Ding! Daughter of Destiny detected: Li Miaoyin. Favorability: -5. Binding successful.]
The System’s notification rang clearly in his mind, sending a jolt through his heart.
Could it finally be her?

He took a deep breath and began ascending the mountain. The temple gate was weathered, the wood scarred by time, yet the air was still faintly scented with incense. Zhang Xian circled the grounds but found no sign of the target the System had indicated. What did catch his attention, however, were several young Taoist acolytes in the courtyard. Each possessed refined and graceful martial technique, already at the pinnacle of the Post-Innate level. And yet, they were barely in their teens.
This temple was no ordinary place.
Zhang Xian stepped forward and asked gently, "Young Fellow Daoist, may I ask if the Abbot is present?"
The young acolyte didn’t even lift his head. "Master is gathering herbs in the back mountains and won't return until evening."

Zhang Xian found a spot to sit and wait. Earlier, he had carefully observed the crowd and confirmed that the Daughter of Destiny was not among the passing villagers. From the extraordinary aura emanating from these young acolytes, Zhang Xian sensed that she must be connected to the temple’s Abbot.
Yet logically speaking, a Taoist temple would never accept female disciples. Could it be...?

As Zhang Xian pondered this possibility, two figures ascended the stone steps. The one behind was a middle-aged Taoist carrying a basket of medicinal herbs, his expression stern. The one ahead was an emaciated old Taoist, his eyebrows frosted with gray, his face etched with countless wrinkles, yet his eyes blazed with vitality. The old Taoist seemed to sense something, his gaze locking onto Zhang Xian from afar.

Zhang Xian’s heart skipped a beat. Both men were masters. The middle-aged man behind was already at the mid-level of the Innate Realm, but even more alarming was the old Taoist ahead. Though his spiritual energy was dwindling to its very limit, there was no doubt—he was a true cultivator!

The old Taoist had clearly detected Zhang Xian’s extraordinary nature as well. "I am Xuanwei, a humble Taoist. Greetings, Fellow Cultivator." His voice was far from aged—it was clear, resonant, and powerful.
Zhang Xian returned the greeting with a respectful bow. "I am Zhang Xian, wandering the lands. My presence here is an intrusion."
The old Taoist showed no reaction, but the middle-aged Taoist behind him suddenly changed his expression, scrutinizing Zhang Xian intently. "You are the Duke of Zhen Guo!"
Zhang Xian replied politely, "Indeed."
Hearing this, the middle-aged Taoist’s expression grew peculiar, yet he said nothing further.
The old Taoist let out a wry smile. "A guest from afar deserves respect. Please, follow me inside for a chat."

The inner chamber of the temple was strikingly simple—a wooden table, two rattan chairs, and several baskets of medicinal herbs tucked into a corner, still fragrant with the fresh scent of newly gathered plants.
The middle-aged Taoist produced a set of coarse pottery tea utensils, boiled water, brewed tea, and remained utterly silent, his gaze occasionally darting furtively toward Zhang Xian.
Having spent years in high positions, Zhang Xian understood that some people simply enjoyed cultivating an air of profound mystery. So he, too, said nothing, quietly sipping his tea.
When he finished his cup, the middle-aged Taoist promptly refilled it.
The atmosphere grew increasingly awkward.
Finally, the middle-aged Taoist broke the silence, as if he had been holding back for far too long. "How is my Senior Sister doing now?"
What?

Zhang Xian stared blankly at the middle-aged Taoist, who continued, looking both aggrieved and exasperated. "My Senior Sister, Yu Rao. I am her Junior Brother, Yu Yun. We fought ten years ago—back then, you knocked me unconscious with a single punch."
Yu Rao was indeed a story from long ago.

Back then, there existed a group calling itself the Holy Sect, whose actions were rather eccentric. Martial artists referred to them as the Demon Sect, but in Zhang Xian’s view, they were merely an unconventional faction.

Originally, this had nothing to do with Zhang Xian. However, the Demon Sect persistently clashed with the sect of his father-in-law, the Sword Saint. Unable to tolerate this, Zhang Xian dealt with them decisively.

Yet he noticed that among the Demon Sect’s ranks was a Holy Maiden named Yu Rao. Her beauty and figure were exceptional, and her martial techniques were as graceful and captivating as a dance—a true feast for the eyes. Thus, he refrained from killing her outright, instead giving her a gentle lesson with a single punch.

Afterward, the Demon Sect regarded this as a profound humiliation. And Yu Rao, as the Demon Sect’s most prominent figure, launched numerous assassination attempts against Zhang Xian. But nothing came of it.

Zhang Xian captured Yu Rao seven times, each time letting her go unharmed. Finally, on the eighth occasion, she surrendered herself entirely, willingly marrying the eighty-year-old Zhang Xian. This scandalous union shocked the entire Great Liang Kingdom, and Zhang Xian endured years of moral condemnation from several prestigious Orthodox sects.
The Holy Sect lost its Holy Maiden, its morale plummeted, and it dissolved, each member going their separate ways.
Zhang Xian never imagined encountering an old acquaintance here. Recalling Yu Rao’s graceful form, he sighed softly. "Yu Rao passed away five years ago."
Hearing this, Yu Yun burst into tears. His lifelong infatuation with his Senior Sister, his eternal moonlight, was now shattered.
As he was still immersed in his grief, a sudden SLAP! sounded. Xuanwei struck him across the face with his dust whisk, sending him flying backward.
"Once you enter my sect, you must purify your six senses! What kind of behavior is this, weeping and wailing like a child?"
To everyone’s surprise, Yu Yun only cried harder, like a child weighing two hundred jin. "Awooo!" he sobbed, gathering the scattered herbs outside and slowly retreating farther away.
Zhang Xian, too, felt deeply moved and fell silent.
For a long while, neither spoke, and the atmosphere became even more awkward.

Xuanwei, however, lacked Zhang Xian’s thick skin. Finally, he sighed and said, "Duke of Zhen Guo, I am not skilled in words, nor do I speak in riddles. I know you have already perfected the Innate Realm and glimpsed the path to cultivation. Yet you can also see how frail I have become, unable to offer you any help."

Hearing this, the middle-aged Taoist’s expression grew peculiar, yet he said nothing further.
The old Taoist let out a wry smile.
"A guest from afar deserves respect.
Please, follow me inside for a chat."

The inner chamber of the temple was strikingly simple—a wooden table, two rattan chairs, and several baskets of medicinal herbs tucked into a corner, still fragrant with the fresh scent of newly gathered plants.
The middle-aged Taoist produced a set of coarse pottery tea utensils, boiled water, brewed tea, and remained utterly silent, his gaze occasionally darting furtively toward Zhang Xian.
Having spent years in high positions, Zhang Xian understood that some people simply enjoyed cultivating an air of profound mystery.
So he, too, said nothing, quietly sipping his tea.
When he finished his cup, the middle-aged Taoist promptly refilled it.
The atmosphere grew increasingly awkward.
Finally, the middle-aged Taoist broke the silence, as if he had been holding back for far too long.
"How is my Senior Sister doing now?"
What?
Zhang Xian stared blankly at the middle-aged Taoist, who continued, looking both aggrieved and exasperated.
"My Senior Sister, Yu Rao.
I am her Junior Brother, Yu Yun.
We fought ten years ago—back then, you knocked me unconscious with a single punch."
Yu Rao was indeed a story from long ago.
Back then, there existed a group calling itself the Holy Sect, whose actions were rather eccentric.
Martial artists referred to them as the Demon Sect, but in Zhang Xian’s view, they were merely an unconventional faction.
Originally, this had nothing to do with Zhang Xian.
However, the Demon Sect persistently clashed with the sect of his father-in-law, the Sword Saint.
Unable to tolerate this, Zhang Xian dealt with them decisively.
Yet he noticed that among the Demon Sect’s ranks was a Holy Maiden named Yu Rao.
Her beauty and figure were exceptional, and her martial techniques were as graceful and captivating as a dance—a true feast for the eyes.
Thus, he refrained from killing her outright, instead giving her a gentle lesson with a single punch.
Afterward, the Demon Sect regarded this as a profound humiliation.
And Yu Rao, as the Demon Sect’s most prominent figure, launched numerous assassination attempts against Zhang Xian.
But nothing came of it.
Zhang Xian captured Yu Rao seven times, each time letting her go unharmed.
Finally, on the eighth occasion, she surrendered herself entirely, willingly marrying the eighty-year-old Zhang Xian.
This scandalous union shocked the entire Great Liang Kingdom, and Zhang Xian endured years of moral condemnation from several prestigious Orthodox sects.
The Holy Sect lost its Holy Maiden, its morale plummeted, and it dissolved, each member going their separate ways.
Zhang Xian never imagined encountering an old acquaintance here.
Recalling Yu Rao’s graceful form, he sighed softly.
"Yu Rao passed away five years ago."
Hearing this, Yu Yun burst into tears.
His lifelong infatuation with his Senior Sister, his eternal moonlight, was now shattered.
As he was still immersed in his grief, a sudden SLAP! sounded.
Xuanwei struck him across the face with his dust whisk, sending him flying backward.
"Once you enter my sect, you must purify your six senses!
What kind of behavior is this, weeping and wailing like a child?"
To everyone’s surprise, Yu Yun only cried harder, like a child weighing two hundred jin.
"Awooo!" he sobbed, gathering the scattered herbs outside and slowly retreating farther away.
Zhang Xian, too, felt deeply moved and fell silent.
For a long while, neither spoke, and the atmosphere became even more awkward.
Xuanwei, however, lacked Zhang Xian’s thick skin.
Finally, he sighed and said, "Duke of Zhen Guo, I am not skilled in words, nor do I speak in riddles.
I know you have already perfected the Innate Realm and glimpsed the path to cultivation.
Yet you can also see how frail I have become, unable to offer you any help."

chapters.title: Chapter 6 Senior Sister, You Died Such a Tragic Death!
paragraphs: Zhang Xian chuckled. This old man spoke with remarkable directness.
"Your insight is truly keen, Daoist Master." Zhang Xian set down his teacup. "I have indeed touched the threshold of cultivation, yet I remain forever unable to cross it."

The old Daoist, Xuanwei, spoke slowly. "Duke of Zhen Guo, you saw just now—my inept disciple has followed me for ten years, yet he has only reached the mid-level of the Innate Realm. As for you, your internal energy is harmonious and complete, just one step away from a breakthrough. But in my view, you lack two crucial things."
"Which two?"
"Spiritual Roots, and the Spiritual Energy of Heaven and Earth."

Xuanwei continued, "If my guess is correct, you lack Spiritual Roots. Otherwise, at your current level, you would have already drawn spiritual energy into your body and reached the initial stage of Qi Refining. Of course, the greater problem lies in this world’s exceedingly thin spiritual energy, rendering cultivation all but impossible. Even if you were to enter the Qi Refining stage, you would be like a tree without roots, a duckweed without water."
As he spoke, Xuanwei gently raised his palm. Wisps of light gathered between his fingers, only to dissipate into nothingness before they could coalesce.
So, besides Spiritual Roots, there is also the issue of ambient spiritual energy.
Zhang Xian, accustomed to overcoming impossible odds, pressed further. "May I ask, Daoist Master, which sect did you originally belong to, and how did you end up here?"

Xuanwei shook his head with a bitter smile. "My sect has long since vanished. Now, I am merely a fallen, wandering cultivator. Look at how depleted my spiritual energy has become—I have reached the end of my road."
Zhang Xian understood that Xuanwei did not wish to elaborate, so he refrained from pressing the matter. Instead, they chatted about trivial subjects for a while.
After a long pause, Zhang Xian rose to leave. Xuanwei also stood to see him off.
Suddenly, without warning, Zhang Xian halted mid-step and asked, "Daoist Master, do you know Li Miaoyin?"
No sooner had the words left his lips than Xuanwei’s aura surged violently.
"Who are you?!" he bellowed.

A massive wave of spiritual pressure swept through the room, overturning every piece of furniture. At the same moment, Xuanwei swung his long sleeve, launching a strike intended to subdue Zhang Xian instantly.
Zhang Xian, however, had anticipated this. He clasped his hands together, meeting Xuanwei’s attack head-on.
BOOM!

The entire room exploded outward. Simultaneously, a streak of silver light whizzed past Zhang Xian. The Ruyi Short Sword pierced directly through Xuanwei's protective spiritual aura, stopping less than half an inch from the Yuzhen acupoint at the back of his neck.
All of this transpired in the blink of an eye.
Xuanwei coughed up a mouthful of blood, his protective aura shattered, his internal organs rattled. "How is this possible... how could you possibly master a magical artifact?"
"Daoist Master, please don't be so agitated. I harbor no ill intentions." Zhang Xian seized the advantage and immediately retreated a safe distance.

Frankly, he had a good impression of Xuanwei, but he hadn't expected such a violent reaction to Li Miaoyin’s name. The old man had lost control instantly. Nor had he anticipated the Ruyi Short Sword would be so formidable. Xuanwei was a Qi Refining stage master, yet his protective aura was like paper before the artifact.
"Old thief, die!"
The middle-aged Taoist, Yu Yun, seeing his master injured, combined old grievances with new fury. His eyes blazed red as he charged forward.
Zhang Xian didn’t even glance at him. He waved his hand, unleashing a gust of internal energy.

Yu Yun flew backward faster than he had come, tumbling several times upon landing. Though uninjured, the humiliation stung worse than any wound. Knowing Zhang Xian had held back, Yu Yun roared, "If you have a grievance, take it out on me! Release my Master!"
The sensation transported him back ten years, to when he had been just as useless, watching his beloved Senior Sister be humiliated by this old thief. And now, his Master too—
That old thief deserves to die!
Zhang Xian, uninterested in further confrontation, glanced at Xuanwei. "Daoist Master, I was merely inquiring about a name. There is no need for such hostility."
He recalled the Ruyi Short Sword, calculating inwardly that with this weapon, handling Xuanwei would pose no difficulty.
Xuanwei, severely wounded, glared fiercely at Zhang Xian. "Where did you hear that name?"
Zhang Xian knew he couldn't explain the System, so he mumbled vaguely, "A friend told me."
"Bullshit!" Xuanwei spat venomously. "Do whatever you want with me—kill me, dismember me!"
With that, he closed his eyes, tilting his neck up in a dramatic gesture of martyrdom.
What is going on?
Zhang Xian certainly wasn't about to kill him. He tried again. "I truly only wanted to inquire about someone."
Unfortunately, Xuanwei had ceased responding, simply lying there with his neck exposed, waiting for the blade.

Meanwhile, Yu Yun scrambled to his feet, rushed forward, was blown back, and rushed forward again. After several failed attempts to get within an inch of Zhang Xian, he collapsed to the ground, weeping bitterly.

"You monster! You tormented my Senior Sister, and now you won't even spare us! What wrong did my Master do to deserve this? Why are you so ruthless? Oh, my Senior Sister, you died such a tragic death!"
The young acolytes in the courtyard watched from a distance, trembling in fear.
Zhang Xian suddenly felt overwhelmed. He felt like a heinous villain bullying the weak, completely contrary to the image he had envisioned.
At that moment, a figure in blue robes descended gracefully from the sky, landing beside Xuanwei.
"I am Li Miaoyin! Who asks for me?"
[Ding! Li Miaoyin’s Favorability toward you is -5. Binding successful.]

The woman was a Taoist nun, approximately forty years old. Her dark hair, streaked with a few strands of silver, was tied loosely in a bun adorned with a plain wooden hairpin. Years had etched fine lines around her eyes, yet they had not dimmed the brightness of her clear, luminous gaze, which still held the delicate beauty of her youth.
A mature woman?
Zhang Xian was somewhat surprised. Li Miaoyin was also a cultivator, seemingly at a slightly higher level than Xuanwei—but not by much.
No big deal.
With the Ruyi Short Sword in hand, Zhang Xian remained completely unfazed. He bowed respectfully. "I am Zhang Xian. I inadvertently injured the Daoist Master earlier. It was purely an accident.
"Could you really injure Xuanwei?" The beautiful woman frowned slightly, a faint line appearing between her brows that added a touch of vitality to her expression.
She turned to Xuanwei. "At your age, you still dare to fight others—and lose, no less!" Though her tone carried a hint of reproach, it could not conceal her concern.
She placed her hand on Xuanwei’s back, transferring spiritual energy to stabilize him.
Seeing Li Miaoyin, Xuanwei’s tone softened instantly. "Senior Sister, I was injured by his magical artifact, but it’s nothing serious. Your spiritual energy—"
"Be quiet!"
Hmm? Something fishy is going on.
Zhang Xian, having navigated the complexities of human relationships for decades, immediately recognized that the bond between these two was far from simple.
"Speak! Why are you seeking me? And injuring Xuanwei—such a thing cannot be excused with a mere apology!" Li Miaoyin demanded, turning her sharp gaze on Zhang Xian.
"Well, a friend told me. They said there was a very powerful cultivator here, and I wanted to make acquaintances."
"Do you think I’d believe such nonsense?"
Zhang Xian knew further fabrication would be futile, so he emphasized, "I truly have no ill intentions."
As he spoke, his internal energy shifted. A streak of silver light flashed briefly, circling the two Taoists before returning to hover beside Zhang Xian.
The unspoken message was clear: Dealing with you both would be effortless. If I truly harbored ill will, I wouldn't be wasting time talking.
Li Miaoyin’s gaze sharpened. A magical artifact! How can a mortal at the Innate level wield a magical artifact? No wonder Xuanwei couldn't defeat him. Even she might not be his match.
Li Miaoyin reflected for a moment. Neither she nor Xuanwei possessed anything worth stealing. Perhaps this man truly meant no harm.
"Stop crying and brew some tea!" Li Miaoyin ordered Yu Yun, who was still sobbing on the ground. Then, supporting Xuanwei, she led him into another room.
The tea room had been destroyed, so they chose the study instead.
Yu Yun, acting as the eternal servant, composed himself, arranged a new tea set, glared sharply at Zhang Xian, and quietly stepped aside.

Xuanwei no longer resembled the ethereal, otherworldly master he once was. He watched Li Miaoyin with aching tenderness. Just now, she had infused her spiritual energy into him, and fine beads of sweat had formed on her forehead.
"Senior Sister, I’m fine now. A few days of rest will suffice," Xuanwei said softly.

Only then did Li Miaoyin release her hand. Seeing the sweat on her forehead, Xuanwei instinctively reached out to wipe it away, but quickly caught himself, pretending nothing had happened. Instead, he cast a scornful glare at Zhang Xian, who was sitting awkwardly opposite them.
"Hmph! To injure me with a magical artifact and still dare to seek out my Senior Sister! Shameless!"
