chapters.title: Chapter 7 Master, Please Come to Your Senses
paragraphs: Across from him, two out of the three people were openly looking down on him, and even Li Miaoyin’s attitude was rather cold. But for Zhang Xian, these were mere trifles.

Back in the day, when he was about to marry the Princess of Daliang, several civil officials in the Grand Hall nearly banged their heads against the pillars in protest, and countless princes and nobles glared at him with murderous intent. Then, when he married the demoness Yu Rao from the Holy Sect, several old-timers from the orthodox sects were ready to slit their own throats, ranting about "purging the righteous path" and "being ashamed to associate with such a person."

As long as you don't feel awkward yourself, it’s always others who end up embarrassed. Over the years, apart from honing his martial skills, what he had really mastered was an iron skin thicker than the city walls. Even as the Duke of Zhen Guo, Zhang Xian was second to none!

Zhang Xian exchanged a few pleasantries with Li Miaoyin. According to her, their story was simple enough: they were both cultivators whose sect had fallen into decline. As Master and Disciple, they had retreated from the world, relying on each other for survival in this obscure Taoist temple for nearly a hundred years. Now that their lifespans were drawing to a close, all they wanted was to spend their remaining days in peace.

But Zhang Xian knew full well they weren’t telling the whole truth. Although Li Miaoyin’s cultivation level was slightly higher than Xuanwei’s, Zhang Xian could sense a severe internal injury lurking within her. If her story were true—if she’d been nursing this injury for a hundred years without healing—it was clear there was much more to it than met the eye.
And the herbs Xuanwei had gathered were no doubt for her use. Yet they were merely common herbs from the mortal realm, offering little more than a token gesture.

Seeing that the atmosphere had eased somewhat, Zhang Xian finally cupped his hands in a respectful bow. "I apologize for any offense I may have caused earlier. Here are ten century-old Snow Ginseng roots, a small token of my apology to Daoist Sister Miaoyin for accidentally harming your Junior Brother."
With a wave of his hand, a box appeared on the ground. The lid sprang open by itself, revealing numerous exquisite compartments filled with Snow Ginseng.
A spatial artifact!
Li Miaoyin and Xuanwei exchanged a glance, their hearts jolted by this unexpected discovery.
Li Miaoyin quickly returned the gesture with a Daoist bow. "Duke Zhen Guo is far too kind. This humble Daoist accepts your gratitude on behalf of Xuanwei."

To ordinary people, these century-old Snow Ginseng roots were incredibly valuable. But to cultivators like them, they were mundane items, their medicinal properties only slightly better than common ginseng.
[Ping! Successfully gifted ten common century-old Snow Ginseng roots. Triggered return: Ten rare Thousand-Year Spirit Ginseng roots.]
Finally, it’s happening again! Zhang Xian’s heart leapt with joy.

Then, he waved his hand once more. Two more boxes appeared on the ground, their lids springing open automatically. The first box gleamed with golden light, neatly stacked with bars of gold. The second box was crammed full of jewels and ornaments.

"These are some mundane treasures—gold, silver, and jewels. My presence just now disturbed your esteemed temple and damaged some of its facilities. Please accept these as compensation for repairs and renovations," Zhang Xian said calmly.
What use could he possibly have for these mundane treasures? Is he insane?
Li Miaoyin felt utterly bewildered. Could it be that the Duke of Zhen Guo is simply mad?

As cultivators, what use do Xuanwei and I have for your mundane wealth? Do you really think we’d cherish such trivial things? And even if you’re giving gold, what’s the meaning of this box of jewels—red coral, pearl crowns, jade ruyi scepters—what kind of rubbish is this?
Li Miaoyin and Xuanwei hurriedly declined, but alas, their combined reluctance couldn’t match Zhang Xian’s thick-skinned persistence. In the end, they had no choice but to accept.
[Ping! Successfully gifted ten thousand taels of gold. Ninety-five percent of it had no effect on Li Miaoyin; five hundred taels triggered a return: Five hundred mid-grade Spirit Stones.]
[Ping! Gift of jewels ineffective. No return.]

Zhang Xian instantly understood—the System wouldn’t return gifts indefinitely. It seemed that only a small portion of this gold would actually benefit Li Miaoyin, perhaps enough to cover her daily needs, while the rest was simply useless to her. As for the box of jewels, it was clearly just thrown in for show.
But it didn’t matter. He had plenty of gold and jewels anyway. This was a steal!

Meanwhile, Xuanwei was secretly grieving. Not only had he been injured today, but he’d also forced Sister Miaoyin to transfer her True Qi to him. This back-and-forth exchange would likely cost both of them several years of their lifespans. Alas!
Behind him, Yu Yun wore an even stranger expression. This old rogue refuses to leave, showering gifts only on Sister Miaoyin—there has to be some ulterior motive.
As he pondered this, he glanced at Zhang Xian, whose face was brimming with eager anticipation. Suddenly, a terrifying suspicion struck him. Could it be...?
His face turned deathly pale in an instant.

"Ahem," Li Miaoyin said hastily, fearing that Zhang Xian would keep giving gifts endlessly. "If the Duke has nothing else to say, perhaps he should come another time. I have evening rituals to attend shortly." She quietly pinched Xuanwei’s arm as she spoke.
Xuanwei understood the hint immediately and managed a faint, blood-streaked smile. "This humble one also needs to stabilize his injuries."
Leave? No way! Not until he’d squeezed every last bit of value out of Li Miaoyin would he ever leave this place.

Zhang Xian flipped his palm, conjuring several glowing stones. "These gems were obtained by chance and are of no use to me. They seem to be exactly the kind of Spirit Stones you mentioned, Daoist Sister. Allow me to present them to you as well."
"Mid-grade Spirit Stones!" Li Miaoyin and Xuanwei exclaimed in unison.
Zhang Xian calmly placed the stones on the table before them. His fingertips still tingled with lingering spiritual energy—freshly produced by the System, still warm to the touch.
Xuanwei murmured, "Sister, these really are mid-grade Spirit Stones!"
His entire body trembled with excitement. With these few stones to nurture her, Sister Miaoyin could recover at least three levels of cultivation and extend her lifespan by another fifty years.
"This is far too precious; we cannot accept it," Li Miaoyin said, her voice trembling. Ten mid-grade Spirit Stones were simply too valuable.

In her former sect, she had reached the peak of Qi Refining and was even a favored disciple personally selected by the Elder. Yet her monthly stipend had never exceeded dozens of low-grade Spirit Stones. One mid-grade stone was worth at least a hundred low-grade ones—and here were ten! Enough to sustain her cultivation for several years!
Zhang Xian took in their reactions carefully. Clearly, these mid-grade Spirit Stones were truly remarkable.

But every gift comes at a price. Zhang Xian smiled slyly and conjured a few more stones from his hand. "These Spirit Stones are of no use to me. Besides, I have plenty more. Daoist Sister Miaoyin, please do not refuse them again."
He still has more?!

Li Miaoyin was shocked. This Zhang Xian possessed attack artifacts, spatial artifacts, and now even an abundance of mid-grade Spirit Stones—such wealth would make even established cultivators envious!
[Ping! Li Miaoyin’s Favorability toward you has increased by 15.]
[Ping! Mid-grade Spirit Stones successfully gifted. The gifted item originated from Li Miaoyin herself (via previous return), so no return can be triggered for her.]
Zhang Xian noted this mentally: It seems I can’t keep milking the same person over and over again. Items originating from a specific target can't be re-gifted to them for a return.
Still, gaining a bit of Favorability wasn’t a loss. Higher Favorability made it easier to continue giving gifts later.

After receiving the Spirit Stones, Xuanwei and Li Miaoyin’s attitudes improved dramatically, completely convinced that Zhang Xian had no malicious intentions. Li Miaoyin’s brow, which had been furrowed for so long, finally relaxed into a rare, charming smile.
For a moment, host and guest were thoroughly delighted—except for Yu Yun.
That old rogue has already set his sights on Sister Miaoyin!
Master, please come to your senses! Danger!!

sentences.text: Across from him, two out of the three people were openly looking down on him, and even Li Miaoyin’s attitude was rather cold.
But for Zhang Xian, these were mere trifles.

Back in the day, when he was about to marry the Princess of Daliang, several civil officials in the Grand Hall nearly banged their heads against the pillars in protest, and countless princes and nobles glared at him with murderous intent.

Then, when he married the demoness Yu Rao from the Holy Sect, several old-timers from the orthodox sects were ready to slit their own throats, ranting about "purging the righteous path" and "being ashamed to associate with such a person."
As long as you don't feel awkward yourself, it’s always others who end up embarrassed.
Over the years, apart from honing his martial skills, what he had really mastered was an iron skin thicker than the city walls.
Even as the Duke of Zhen Guo, Zhang Xian was second to none!
Zhang Xian exchanged a few pleasantries with Li Miaoyin.
According to her, their story was simple enough: they were both cultivators whose sect had fallen into decline.
As Master and Disciple, they had retreated from the world, relying on each other for survival in this obscure Taoist temple for nearly a hundred years.
Now that their lifespans were drawing to a close, all they wanted was to spend their remaining days in peace.
But Zhang Xian knew full well they weren’t telling the whole truth.
Although Li Miaoyin’s cultivation level was slightly higher than Xuanwei’s, Zhang Xian could sense a severe internal injury lurking within her.
If her story were true—if she’d been nursing this injury for a hundred years without healing—it was clear there was much more to it than met the eye.
And the herbs Xuanwei had gathered were no doubt for her use.
Yet they were merely common herbs from the mortal realm, offering little more than a token gesture.
Seeing that the atmosphere had eased somewhat, Zhang Xian finally cupped his hands in a respectful bow.
"I apologize for any offense I may have caused earlier.
Here are ten century-old Snow Ginseng roots, a small token of my apology to Daoist Sister Miaoyin for accidentally harming your Junior Brother."
With a wave of his hand, a box appeared on the ground.
The lid sprang open by itself, revealing numerous exquisite compartments filled with Snow Ginseng.
A spatial artifact!
Li Miaoyin and Xuanwei exchanged a glance, their hearts jolted by this unexpected discovery.
Li Miaoyin quickly returned the gesture with a Daoist bow.
"Duke Zhen Guo is far too kind.
This humble Daoist accepts your gratitude on behalf of Xuanwei."
To ordinary people, these century-old Snow Ginseng roots were incredibly valuable.
But to cultivators like them, they were mundane items, their medicinal properties only slightly better than common ginseng.
[Ping!
Successfully gifted ten common century-old Snow Ginseng roots.
Triggered return: Ten rare Thousand-Year Spirit Ginseng roots.]
Finally, it’s happening again!
Zhang Xian’s heart leapt with joy.
Then, he waved his hand once more.
Two more boxes appeared on the ground, their lids springing open automatically.
The first box gleamed with golden light, neatly stacked with bars of gold.
The second box was crammed full of jewels and ornaments.
"These are some mundane treasures—gold, silver, and jewels.
My presence just now disturbed your esteemed temple and damaged some of its facilities.
Please accept these as compensation for repairs and renovations," Zhang Xian said calmly.
What use could he possibly have for these mundane treasures?
Is he insane?
Li Miaoyin felt utterly bewildered.
Could it be that the Duke of Zhen Guo is simply mad?
As cultivators, what use do Xuanwei and I have for your mundane wealth?
Do you really think we’d cherish such trivial things?
And even if you’re giving gold, what’s the meaning of this box of jewels—red coral, pearl crowns, jade ruyi scepters—what kind of rubbish is this?
Li Miaoyin and Xuanwei hurriedly declined, but alas, their combined reluctance couldn’t match Zhang Xian’s thick-skinned persistence.
In the end, they had no choice but to accept.
[Ping!
Successfully gifted ten thousand taels of gold.
Ninety-five percent of it had no effect on Li Miaoyin; five hundred taels triggered a return: Five hundred mid-grade Spirit Stones.]
[Ping!
Gift of jewels ineffective.
No return.]
Zhang Xian instantly understood—the System wouldn’t return gifts indefinitely.
It seemed that only a small portion of this gold would actually benefit Li Miaoyin, perhaps enough to cover her daily needs, while the rest was simply useless to her.
As for the box of jewels, it was clearly just thrown in for show.
But it didn’t matter.
He had plenty of gold and jewels anyway.
This was a steal!
Meanwhile, Xuanwei was secretly grieving.
Not only had he been injured today, but he’d also forced Sister Miaoyin to transfer her True Qi to him.
This back-and-forth exchange would likely cost both of them several years of their lifespans.
Alas!
Behind him, Yu Yun wore an even stranger expression.
This old rogue refuses to leave, showering gifts only on Sister Miaoyin—there has to be some ulterior motive.
As he pondered this, he glanced at Zhang Xian, whose face was brimming with eager anticipation.
Suddenly, a terrifying suspicion struck him.
Could it be...?
His face turned deathly pale in an instant.
"Ahem," Li Miaoyin said hastily, fearing that Zhang Xian would keep giving gifts endlessly.
"If the Duke has nothing else to say, perhaps he should come another time.
I have evening rituals to attend shortly." She quietly pinched Xuanwei’s arm as she spoke.
Xuanwei understood the hint immediately and managed a faint, blood-streaked smile.
"This humble one also needs to stabilize his injuries."
Leave?
No way!
Not until he’d squeezed every last bit of value out of Li Miaoyin would he ever leave this place.
Zhang Xian flipped his palm, conjuring several glowing stones.
"These gems were obtained by chance and are of no use to me.
They seem to be exactly the kind of Spirit Stones you mentioned, Daoist Sister.
Allow me to present them to you as well."
"Mid-grade Spirit Stones!" Li Miaoyin and Xuanwei exclaimed in unison.
Zhang Xian calmly placed the stones on the table before them.
His fingertips still tingled with lingering spiritual energy—freshly produced by the System, still warm to the touch.
Xuanwei murmured, "Sister, these really are mid-grade Spirit Stones!"
His entire body trembled with excitement.
With these few stones to nurture her, Sister Miaoyin could recover at least three levels of cultivation and extend her lifespan by another fifty years.
"This is far too precious; we cannot accept it," Li Miaoyin said, her voice trembling.
Ten mid-grade Spirit Stones were simply too valuable.
In her former sect, she had reached the peak of Qi Refining and was even a favored disciple personally selected by the Elder.
Yet her monthly stipend had never exceeded dozens of low-grade Spirit Stones.
One mid-grade stone was worth at least a hundred low-grade ones—and here were ten!
Enough to sustain her cultivation for several years!
Zhang Xian took in their reactions carefully.
Clearly, these mid-grade Spirit Stones were truly remarkable.
But every gift comes at a price.
Zhang Xian smiled slyly and conjured a few more stones from his hand.
"These Spirit Stones are of no use to me.
Besides, I have plenty more.
Daoist Sister Miaoyin, please do not refuse them again."
He still has more?!
Li Miaoyin was shocked.
This Zhang Xian possessed attack artifacts, spatial artifacts, and now even an abundance of mid-grade Spirit Stones—such wealth would make even established cultivators envious!
[Ping!
Li Miaoyin’s Favorability toward you has increased by 15.]
[Ping!
Mid-grade Spirit Stones successfully gifted.
The gifted item originated from Li Miaoyin herself (via previous return), so no return can be triggered for her.]
Zhang Xian noted this mentally: It seems I can’t keep milking the same person over and over again.
Items originating from a specific target can't be re-gifted to them for a return.
Still, gaining a bit of Favorability wasn’t a loss.
Higher Favorability made it easier to continue giving gifts later.
After receiving the Spirit Stones, Xuanwei and Li Miaoyin’s attitudes improved dramatically, completely convinced that Zhang Xian had no malicious intentions.
Li Miaoyin’s brow, which had been furrowed for so long, finally relaxed into a rare, charming smile.
For a moment, host and guest were thoroughly delighted—except for Yu Yun.
That old rogue has already set his sights on Sister Miaoyin!
Master, please come to your senses!
Danger!!

chapters.title: Chapter 8 It’s You Who’s Green
paragraphs: Xuanwei was currently immersed in the joy of finally seeing Sister Miaoyin’s injuries healing, completely oblivious to his disciple’s contorted expression.
Li Miaoyin, however, noticed Yu Yun’s unusual demeanor. She simply assumed he was overwhelmed by Zhang Xian’s extravagance and gently beckoned him over.
"It’s getting late. Duke Zhen Guo, why don’t you stay at our temple tonight? Yu Yun, go prepare a side room for him."
Yu Yun’s heart screamed inwardly: This is inviting the wolf into the sheepfold!
This old rogue definitely has no good intentions!
He must be after Sister Miaoyin!
Master, wake up!
Before leaving, he glared fiercely at Zhang Xian.
Zhang Xian: ?
Is this guy still looking down on me because of Yu Rao? Forget it—it doesn’t matter. He continued chatting casually with Li Miaoyin and Xuanwei.
"Speaking of which, Daoist Sister Miaoyin, I have another request, albeit an awkward one."
"Please speak freely, Daoist Brother."

Zhang Xian took out a book titled The Secret Art of Condensing a Golden Core and handed it to Li Miaoyin. "I came across this book by chance and would like to gift it to you. Your insight far surpasses mine. I hope you can help me interpret it."

Fearing the System might not recognize the transfer, he quickly added, "This book takes an unconventional approach, using a ‘False Core’ as a gateway to cultivation. It contains many valuable insights that should inspire your practice as well."
Li Miaoyin hadn’t expected such a simple request. She flipped through The Secret Art of Condensing a Golden Core and immediately understood its essence.

For ordinary people without Spiritual Roots to seek cultivation was a perennial topic in the cultivation world. Yet Spiritual Roots were like an insurmountable chasm, blocking the dreams of most mortals. As far as Li Miaoyin knew, the cultivation world still hadn’t found a mature solution.

Admittedly, some top-tier sects and families possessed special methods to guide ordinary people onto the path, but these were either closely guarded secrets or dangerous, cursed techniques with endless repercussions. Even when such methods existed, the resources required were astronomical—far greater than nurturing a prodigy.
I can’t help him!
Li Miaoyin felt regretful but couldn’t bear to bluntly disappoint him. "I’ll accept this book, Duke Zhen Guo. You’re far too kind. We cultivators should support each other."
[Ping! Successfully gifted the common Secret Art of Condensing a Golden Core. Triggered return: The rare Classic of Nurturing Golden Cores with Azure Wood.]
This is promising!

The group chatted for a long time afterward. Xuanwei was in exceptionally good spirits. He hadn’t felt this happy in a century, practically dying to share all his cultivation experiences with Zhang Xian.
At night, in the guest room.
Zhang Xian sat cross-legged on a meditation cushion, his lips curling into an ecstatic grin.
The Classic of Nurturing Golden Cores with Azure Wood!

The cultivation technique unfolded slowly in his mind, each character a pearl of wisdom, profoundly mysterious and complete—a method for nurturing a Golden Core far superior to The Secret Art of Condensing a Golden Core.

This technique used Wood-element spiritual energy to nourish the body. It not only aided in the formation of a False Core but also planted a strand of endlessly renewing Azure Wood Energy within the body, effectively creating an artificial Wood Spirit Root. Cultivating this technique to perfection could allow one to reach the False Core stage, with power nearly equivalent to that of a true Golden Core cultivator.
However, this technique required an enormous amount of Wood-element Spirit Stones—more than ten times the usual amount for a regular cultivator.
Yet to enable an ordinary mortal to embark on the path of cultivation, even if only as a False Core, was nothing short of a miraculous technique.

Zhang Xian immediately began practicing. His internal energy flowed gently through his body. At the same time, he took out two mid-grade Wood-element Spirit Stones, holding them in his hands and following the method outlined in the Classic. He circulated the energy throughout his body.

Slowly, a vibrant, emerald-green "False Core" began to condense in his dantian. Every pore on his body opened wide, as if soaking in a hot spring. Even his graying temples seemed to glow faintly with new vitality.
By the time dawn broke, the "False Core" in his dantian had grown from the size of a grain of rice to the size of a soybean.

Zhang Xian was overjoyed. At this rate, in less than half a month, he could fully master the first level of the Classic, and with the aid of his False Core, successfully refine Qi and step onto the path of cultivation!
The System is amazing!
Zhang Xian, feeling refreshed and invigorated, pushed open the door—and collided head-on with Yu Yun, whose eyes were ringed with dark circles.
Zhang Xian greeted him with a cheerful smile. "Daoist Brother Yu Yun, good morning! Have you seen your beloved Sister Miaoyin yet? I must thank her properly!"
Yu Yun’s lips twitched uncontrollably. He spat out bitterly, "I don’t know!" before quickly turning away.
That wretched Duke of Zhen Guo, coming to find Sister Miaoyin first thing in the morning—does he not even bother to pretend anymore?

"Pah!" A whisk brushed Yu Yun’s face—a signal from Xuanwei, already dressed and looking remarkably energetic, completely unlike someone who had just suffered an injury. "You lack manners! Go brew tea in the study."
"Good morning, Duke Zhen Guo. I spent the entire night studying The Secret Art of Condensing a Golden Core and gained some insights. Let’s discuss it further in the study."
Waaah!

Seeing Master Xuanwei smiling like a simpleton broke Yu Yun’s heart even more. In his mind, he recalled Sister Miaoyin’s graceful figure, feeling as though Master Xuanwei had become his younger self—naive and oblivious.
Master, please wake up! You don’t yet know what you’re about to lose!
That old rogue, the Duke of Zhen Guo, deserves to die!
"Duke Zhen Guo, I notice your cultivation level has improved overnight. Congratulations!"
"A slight increase, all thanks to Daoist Brother Xuanwei. Listening to your insights was like enlightenment itself, deeply benefiting me. I’m endlessly grateful."
Xuanwei’s face lit up even brighter, and he immediately took out a communication talisman to summon Sister Li Miaoyin.
When Li Miaoyin pushed open the door, Zhang Xian’s eyes widened in admiration.

She wore a simple white Daoist robe, her black hair cascading like a waterfall, her features painted like a masterpiece. Her skin glowed faintly with a jade-like luster in the morning light. Her posture was even more upright than yesterday, and her every movement exuded an ethereal aura, yet also carried a lively charm unique to young women.
Truly a woman destined by the System—her beauty alone was beyond compare.
"S-Sister?!" Xuanwei stammered, nearly tripping over his own robe.
How many years has it been? How many years has he gone without seeing Sister Miaoyin’s youthful beauty, only to see her rejuvenated overnight?
Li Miaoyin smiled softly, her eyes sparkling with a long-lost playfulness. "What’s wrong? Don’t you recognize me anymore?"
Yu Yun’s heart shattered completely.
He looked at his rejuvenated Sister Miaoyin, then at Zhang Xian, who was equally stunned.
It’s over!
Sister Miaoyin has become younger!
That old rogue, the Duke of Zhen Guo, will surely be even more excited now!
"Congratulations, Daoist Sister," Zhang Xian said with a respectful bow. He could tell that Sister Miaoyin’s injuries had healed somewhat, and her cultivation level had risen compared to yesterday.
"Thanks to the Duke’s Spirit Stones," Li Miaoyin replied solemnly. These stones were like a second life for both her and Xuanwei.
"I see wisps of spiritual energy circulating within the Duke’s body. It seems he’s made significant progress," Li Miaoyin remarked, glancing at Zhang Xian with surprise.
She never imagined Zhang Xian could achieve such remarkable progress overnight. Could he really succeed in refining Qi?
"Indeed. Wood element nurtures growth. I plan to start with the Wood element, using the power of Spirit Stones to condense a False Core."

"The Duke’s idea is brilliant! The Wood element corresponds to the Azure Dragon in the East, symbolizing burgeoning vitality. I see your internal energy flowing endlessly, brimming with green energy. Truly commendable!" Xuanwei added with a smile.
Yu Yun’s heart ached terribly.
Master, please stop talking! It’s not him who’s green—it’s you!

chapters.title: Chapter 9 Four Generations Weep Together, Embracing Each Other
paragraphs: In the days that followed, Zhang Xian remained at the Taoist temple. Aside from seeking guidance from Xuanwei and Li Miaoyin, he spent all his time practicing the Classic of Nurturing Golden Cores with Azure Wood. Finally, on the evening of the ninth day, a vortex the size of an egg yolk formed in his dantian, signifying the completion of his False Core!
The first level of the Classic was now fully mastered!

At the same time, a faint green aura began to emanate from Zhang Xian’s body—clear evidence of the Wood Spirit Root energy he had cultivated. The surrounding spiritual energy started flowing freely throughout his being, drawn by the power of his False Core. This verdant energy traveled along his meridians, and wherever it passed, his withered organs seemed to sprout tender buds, emitting a soft rustling sound like seedlings breaking through the earth. Even his facial features gradually regained their youthful vitality.
As dawn approached, Zhang Xian exhaled a deep breath of stale air.
Qi Refining has been achieved!
At this moment, his five senses were extraordinarily sharp, so much so that he could clearly see the dewdrops clinging to pine needles a hundred meters away.
Is this what cultivators call spiritual perception?

He concentrated further, carefully sensing the energies around him. Indeed, Li Miaoyin’s aura was the strongest within the temple, followed closely by Xuanwei’s. Both were cultivators of the Water attribute. The other disciples in the temple, including Yu Yun, also possessed Spirit Roots, but none of them had any trace of spiritual energy within them.

Zhang Xian closed his eyes, immersing himself completely in his newfound perception. Soon, he sensed Li Miaoyin and Xuanwei approaching together. A faint smile crossed his lips as he opened the door to welcome his guests.
From quite a distance, he already heard Xuanwei’s hearty, booming laughter. "Hahaha!"
"Earlier, my Senior Sister and I both sensed a spiritual presence enveloping the area. It must be Lord Zhen Guo who has successfully completed Qi Refining! What joyful news!"

Zhang Xian returned the gesture with a respectful bow. "This achievement would have been impossible without the generous assistance of both of you esteemed friends. If I had tried to cultivate alone behind closed doors, I never could have succeeded."

Xuanwei genuinely believed the credit belonged entirely to himself, feeling deeply honored and laughing even louder. Yet, not far behind the two of them, Yu Yun watched Lord Zhen Guo’s youthful and handsome face, his heart growing ever more bitter.
Oh no! That old rogue, Lord Zhen Guo, has broken through to the Qi Refining stage, gaining centuries of lifespan out of thin air! Truly a calamity that will haunt us for millennia!
Finally, two months later, Yu Yun could bear it no longer. Taking advantage of an opportunity to go out shopping, he pulled Xuanwei aside and pleaded bitterly, "Master! We’re doomed!"
"What do you mean ‘doomed’? Who’s doomed?"

Xuanwei had been in exceptionally good spirits these past few days. His Senior Sister had already recovered to the sixth level of Qi Refining thanks to the Spirit Stones. Xuanwei himself no longer needed to transfer his True Qi to sustain her life, as he had done every year before. Not only had his years of drained cultivation been fully restored, but he even stood a chance to break through to the next level!
"It’s that old rogue, Zhang Xian! He’s clearly coveting Senior Sister Miaoyin!" Yu Yun cried out, his voice filled with anguish.
"Impossible! Lord Zhen Guo has saved both my Senior Sister and me! Never utter such words again!
"You simply don’t understand Lord Zhen Guo’s true nature, Master!" Yu Yun said, pulling a book titled Wild Chronicles of Great Liang from his chest, his fingers trembling slightly. "Look here—"

Lord Zhen Guo, Zhang Xian, is over ninety years old and maintains eighteen beautiful concubines in his residence. In the past ten years, six out of ten entries in the Great Liang Records of Beautiful Prodigies have ended up as his wives.
Yu Yun couldn’t help but recall that rainy night when he learned that his Senior Sister, Yu Rao, was to marry Zhang Xian.

His grandfather, once a renowned swordsman in the martial world, had been equally famous as the daughter of the Sword Sage. Yet he had loved her deeply for years without success, only to see her marry that very same rogue, Zhang Xian. Overcome with rage, he vowed never to wield a sword again.

This indirectly led his son—Yu Yun’s father—to abandon his martial heritage and pursue officialdom instead. His father fell in love with two twin sisters, both celebrated courtesans in the capital. The younger sister was gentle and demure, while the elder was lively and spirited. After agonizing over his choice for half a year, he realized he favored the younger sister more. But then, to his utter despair, he discovered that Zhang Xian had tricked both sisters into marrying him! Consumed by fury, he leapt into the river, nearly drowning.

Then there was Yu Yun’s own uncle, who likewise abandoned martial arts for scholarly pursuits, quickly earning high honors. At a banquet, he caught a fleeting glimpse of the Imperial Princess, instantly captivated by her ethereal beauty. Determined to become her consort, he redoubled his efforts.

But after a tumultuous upheaval, the Princess too ended up married to that very same old villain! Zhang Xian, a brute of immense strength, and the Princess, still so young! How could she possibly endure such abuse? How could that villain bring himself to do such a thing?!
And finally, there was his own tragic story with his Senior Sister, which he chose not to elaborate upon.

That rainy night, he sat at home, heartbroken and drunk, while his grandfather and father tried to comfort him. But as they spoke, each of them was reminded of their own painful memories, and soon the four generations—grandfather, father, Yu Yun, and the memory of his Senior Sister—were weeping together in the rain, cursing that old villain with heartbreaking grief.

Xuanwei paused, then replied, "Loving beautiful women isn’t a flaw. Besides, my Senior Sister and I share a deep bond, having endured hardships together for over a century. Yu Yun, please stop speaking like this."
"You underestimate just how low that old rogue, Zhang Xian, will sink, Master!" Yu Yun retorted, flipping another page.
In the tenth year of Emperor Liang Jing’s reign, Lord Zhen Guo led troops on a western expedition, assassinating the Grassland King and forcibly seizing his Queen as his own wife.

Xuanwei took a deep breath, seized the book, and flipped through several pages. He found nothing but tales of Zhang Xian’s romantic escapades, some of which were even too scandalous to describe, causing him to shudder involuntarily.

Yu Yun seized the moment, pressing his advantage. "Master, that Lord Zhen Guo is nothing short of an ancient demon! Remember how, from the very beginning, he inquired about Senior Sister Miaoyin’s name? Clearly, he had his sights set squarely on her!"
"And recently, he’s been sending you Spirit Stones—this is his usual tactic! First, he sweet-talks you with gifts, then, after a few days, he reveals his true colors!"

Suddenly, Xuanwei felt the Spirit Stones in his hand grow unbearably hot. Recalling his Senior Sister’s exquisite beauty, he was confident in her resilience, but what if Zhang Xian resorted to force? With his magical artifacts at the ready, they stood no chance against him! Could it really be that he harbored designs on his Senior Sister?
"I’ll go speak with my Senior Sister."
Watching Xuanwei walk away, Yu Yun finally felt a great weight lifted from his heart.
Now that I’ve exposed your true nature, old villain, you’ll never lay a hand on Senior Sister Miaoyin again!
Meanwhile, Zhang Xian sat cross-legged in a bamboo grove on the back mountain of the Taoist temple.
Two months had passed since he broke through to the Qi Refining stage, and now he had reached the third level.

Because Great Liang lacked spiritual energy, and because he practiced the Classic of Nurturing Golden Cores with Azure Wood, his consumption of spiritual energy was more than ten times greater than that of ordinary cultivators.

Reaching this level had already cost him sixty medium-grade Wood Spirit Stones, not counting those he had previously given to Xuanwei and Li Miaoyin. Now, he had only thirty-five Wood Spirit Stones remaining in his storage space, along with roughly three hundred and fifty other types.
If the attributes didn’t match, the cultivation effect was reduced by half. These remaining stones, at best, would only suffice for him to reach the sixth level of Qi Refining.
These past few days, Zhang Xian had again tentatively offered Li Miaoyin some Spirit Stones and other supplies, but received nothing in return.
There was nothing else she needed beyond medium-grade Spirit Stones, and the stones generated by his System couldn’t be gifted to the same person and then returned through a loophole.
Zhang Xian was growing increasingly eager to enter the cultivation world, realizing he needed to bind himself to more Destined Women and cast a wider net.

In recent days, Xuanwei and Li Miaoyin had also enlightened him about the cultivation world. They explained that Great Liang was merely a fragment of the greater world, a self-contained miniature universe.
The cultivation world they spoke of, however, was a vast, expansive realm, brimming with spiritual energy, teeming with sects, and hundreds of times larger than Great Liang’s miniature universe.

Because Great Liang’s miniature universe lacked spiritual energy, no one paid it any attention, making it essentially unclaimed territory. To return from this miniature universe to the greater world, one needed to construct a powerful spiritual energy conduit—a ritual array capable of connecting the two realms. Fortunately, this ritual had no technical barriers, though it was exceedingly expensive, requiring ten medium-grade Spirit Stones for a single journey.
As Zhang Xian pondered these matters, he suddenly sensed two figures rapidly approaching, holding hands and walking side by side.

One of them was Li Miaoyin herself, whose appearance had transformed utterly compared to just a few months ago. Her eyebrows resembled distant mountains veiled in mist, her lips were as red as cinnabar, and her figure was graceful and elegant—she was now a truly stunning woman.
Yet what surprised Zhang Xian most was that Li Miaoyin was accompanied by a young Taoist priest, seemingly in his twenties, with skin as white as jade and a breathtakingly handsome face.
Who on earth is this? Is he Li Miaoyin’s secret young lover?
The two landed nearby. Li Miaoyin’s cheeks flushed slightly, while the young man beside her wore a confident smile.
"Lord Zhen Guo."
"Xuanwei???" Zhang Xian exclaimed in astonishment.

chapters.title: Chapter 10 Finally Switched to the Official Map
paragraphs: Xuanwei seemed quite pleased by Zhang Xian’s astonishment. A faint smile tugged at the corners of his lips as he reached up to stroke his smooth chin. "Thanks to the Duke of the Nation, my cultivation has made a breakthrough, so I’ve naturally regained the appearance of my youth.
"Hehe, now that you’ve seen this breathtakingly handsome face of mine, you must know who my Senior Sister truly loves best," he said, gently squeezing Li Miaoyin’s delicate hand.

Li Miaoyin felt slightly shy. Yesterday, Xuanwei had sought her out and shared Yu Yun’s analysis with her. As the person directly involved, Li Miaoyin hadn’t sensed any improper intentions from Zhang Xian toward her at all.
However, she’d received so much kindness from him lately that she decided it was time to clarify her feelings, lest things become awkward in the future. And so, this scene unfolded.

Having spent so many years in the Great Liang Kingdom, Zhang Xian’s romantic life was far richer than theirs. He immediately understood their intentions, though he found it rather amusing. It seemed he’d given them too much generosity, leading to unnecessary misunderstandings.
Zhang Xian didn’t call them out directly, but politely remarked, "I simply never imagined Daoist Brother Xuanwei would be so radiant and dashing—no wonder Daoist Sister Miaoyin is so captivated."
Li Miaoyin’s face flushed even deeper, and she shot Xuanwei a reproachful glance. "What sour grapes are you eating? If Zhang Xian truly had ulterior motives, would he say something like this?"
"I’ve noticed your progress has been astonishing these past few days. I suspect you’ve achieved another breakthrough," Li Miaoyin quickly changed the subject.
"I’ve already reached the third stage of Qi Refining."

The two were somewhat shocked. In this small world where spiritual energy had long since vanished, Zhang Xian had managed to forcefully cultivate himself all the way to the third stage of Qi Refining. Clearly, he possessed quite a few Spirit Stones.
If they knew that the resources Zhang Xian had consumed were actually ten times greater than what he claimed, they’d likely be utterly dumbfounded.
"I plan to stabilize my current realm for a while, and then head to the grand cultivation world in about half a month," Zhang Xian continued.
Both Li Miaoyin and Xuanwei had long known about Zhang Xian’s plans, but they hadn’t expected it to happen so soon.

Li Miaoyin cautioned, "The grand cultivation world is vastly different from the Great Liang Kingdom. It’s a place where danger and opportunity coexist. Daoist Brother, please be cautious. And once you arrive there, it’s best not to reveal your origins. This world has completely run out of spiritual energy; if someone discovers your background, they’ll surely investigate and covet you, causing unnecessary trouble."
Zhang Xian thought to himself, If that wretched Nangong Yao recognizes me, I’m finished. Though I’ve already concealed my name, I’ll also have to alter my appearance significantly.
Thinking this, he nodded and said, "Thank you for your advice, Daoist Sister. Actually, I’d like to ask you something else. Have you ever heard of the Yunmiao Sect?"
Hearing this, both of them felt a chill in their hearts.

"The Yunmiao Sect is one of the top two major sects in our Southern Region. It has countless disciples, and its jurisdiction alone is more than a hundred times larger than the Great Liang Kingdom. It even has hundreds of affiliated sects under its umbrella.

"Senior Sister and I were originally cultivators of the Shuiyun Sect, an affiliated sect of the Yunmiao Sect. I came from a background as a wandering cultivator, while Senior Sister Li’s family held some influence within the Shuiyun Sect. Among these affiliated sects, those with exceptional talent are usually sent to the Yunmiao Sect for cultivation. Senior Sister was exceptionally gifted and originally had the chance to join the Yunmiao Sect, but I ended up dragging her down."
As he spoke these words, Xuanwei’s expression filled with guilt, while Li Miaoyin smiled softly and linked her arm through his.

"Back then, Senior Sister and I were deeply in love. But the branch of the Yunmiao Sect that wanted to accept her as a disciple practiced a special Water-based cultivation technique—one that required maintaining a pure, unblemished state and severing all emotional ties. Senior Sister refused to do that."
"At the time, the pressure was immense. I almost gave up myself, but Senior Sister was so stubborn that she ultimately fell out with her family and secretly pledged her life to me."

"Because of this, Senior Sister was punished by her family, stripped of her cultivation, and I was expelled from the sect. The Li family even sent people to hunt me down. With no other choice, Senior Sister and I fled to this small world and have remained here ever since."
Li Miaoyin added calmly, "Actually, the Yunmiao Sect didn’t pursue the matter back then. It was just the Li family’s fear of offending the Yunmiao Sect."

"But after all these years, my brother and I have long since let go of it. My family gave me life and raised me, and later stripped me of my cultivation—those debts are settled. As for the Yunmiao Sect’s cultivation technique, which demands severing all emotional ties—if I can’t stay with my brother, then there’s no point in pursuing cultivation anyway."
As she finished speaking, the two intertwined their fingers tightly, gazing into each other’s eyes with deep affection.
Zhang Xian, suddenly bombarded with such romantic vibes, felt overwhelmed. He never would have guessed Li Miaoyin was such a hopeless romantic.
After offering a few comforting words, Zhang Xian pressed on, "Have you ever heard of someone named Nangong Yao from the Yunmiao Sect? She's probably a Senior Elder or something similar."

"We’ve never heard of her. My cultivation is too low to come into contact with figures of such high rank. However, in Tianmu City, which falls under the jurisdiction of the Yunmiao Sect, there’s a Nangong family. You should be able to find out more there."
Zhang Xian silently made a note of this.

Li Miaoyin and Xuanwei knew Zhang Xian had many secrets, but since he wasn’t sharing them, they wouldn’t pry either. Still, they expressed some concern: "Daoist Brother, neither the Yunmiao Sect nor the Nangong family is someone you should provoke right now."
"Oh, why would I? To be honest, all my cultivation treasures are thanks to the Yunmiao Sect. I’m here precisely to pay my respects and express my gratitude," Zhang Xian replied without flinching.
Half a year later, in the grand cultivation world, five hundred li outside the Shuiyun Sect.

This was a spiritually auspicious mine located in a shaded mountain area, where scattered cultivators were busy digging with mining hoes. Among them, one figure stood out particularly—a figure dressed in goose-yellow.

She wore a short, cross-collared jacket, her wrists slender as jade, and a knee-length, pale apricot-colored skirt whose hem rippled like waves, revealing a pair of exquisitely shaped calves wrapped in snow-white socks. Right now, she was bent over, gripping her mining pickaxe, her fingertips tinged pink, her face delicate and petite, wisps of hair plastered to her reddened cheeks by sweat.

Every time she bent down to dig, the neckline of her garment would slightly open, revealing the gentle rise and fall of her chest, and the sleek lines of her calves beneath the white socks, alternately taut and relaxed.

At this moment, she was murmuring softly, her tongue unconsciously brushing her lower lip, deepening the already vibrant hue of her lips. A single bead of sweat hung precariously from her chin, suspended halfway between falling and staying put.
This sight left several nearby male cultivators utterly entranced.
"Today, Sister Yinyin is so beautiful! Especially her thighs, barely hidden beneath that short skirt!"

Seemingly exhausted from digging, the lovely woman sat directly on the spiritual ore, raising both arms high and stretching luxuriously. This movement caused her already slender frame to unfurl completely.

The apricot-colored jacket was pulled upward by her motion, exposing a stretch of waist as smooth and luminous as jade, dotted with fine beads of sweat that shimmered delicately in the sunlight. Her body also tightened with the movement, outlining the soft curves of her youthful hips and waist.
Gulp. Several male cultivators couldn’t help but swallow hard.
Her name was Lin Yinyin, the undisputed "Mining Flower" of this very mine.

After catching her breath for a moment, she pulled a flask of spiritual spring water from her bosom and took two hearty gulps. Then, she handed the flask to a nearby male cultivator who seemed somewhat distracted, her voice sweet and coy.
"Senior Brother Song, you must be tired too, would you like some?"

The male cultivator instantly became agitated, instinctively glancing at Lin Yinyin’s cherry-red lips before nervously taking the flask and quickly drinking two sips, finding today’s spiritual spring water especially sweet.
"I’ve indirectly kissed Sister Yinyin! I’m so happy!"
With a casual flick of her fingers, Lin Yinyin swept her loose strands of hair behind her ear. How effortlessly charming!

The apricot-colored jacket was pulled upward by her motion, exposing a stretch of waist as smooth and luminous as jade, dotted with fine beads of sweat that shimmered delicately in the sunlight.
Her body also tightened with the movement, outlining the soft curves of her youthful hips and waist.
Gulp.
Several male cultivators couldn’t help but swallow hard.
Her name was Lin Yinyin, the undisputed "Mining Flower" of this very mine.
After catching her breath for a moment, she pulled a flask of spiritual spring water from her bosom and took two hearty gulps.
Then, she handed the flask to a nearby male cultivator who seemed somewhat distracted, her voice sweet and coy.
"Senior Brother Song, you must be tired too, would you like some?"

The male cultivator instantly became agitated, instinctively glancing at Lin Yinyin’s cherry-red lips before nervously taking the flask and quickly drinking two sips, finding today’s spiritual spring water especially sweet.
"I’ve indirectly kissed Sister Yinyin!
I’m so happy!"
With a casual flick of her fingers, Lin Yinyin swept her loose strands of hair behind her ear.
How effortlessly charming!

chapters.title: Chapter 11 Sister Yinyin Is Just Wonderful in Every Way
paragraphs: The male cultivator, whom Lin Yinyin called Senior Brother Song, took a few sips of water, as if he had finally made up his mind.
"Yinyin," he said earnestly, "I've already excavated the core containing the spirit ore. You take it and refine it."
"Ah? How could I possibly accept this?" Lin Yinyin exclaimed, her eyes widening. "This spirit ore was painstakingly mined by you over five whole days! What will you do if I take it?"
"Don't worry about it. I've been lucky lately. I noticed another potential mining spot over there—I feel like I can dig up even more spirit ore in just a few days."

"No, no way! Here's what we'll do, Senior Brother Song. I'll take this spirit ore to refine it. I estimate it will yield at least ten low-grade Spirit Stones. I'll take just a few of them—just to share in your good fortune. Oh, and yesterday I saw a mining pick that can sense Geng Metal energy. I'm going to buy it and give it to you as a gift. That way, we can mine together and accumulate even more Spirit Stones!"
Hearing Lin Yinyin's soft, sweet voice, Senior Brother Song became even more agitated with excitement.
Sister Yinyin is truly so considerate! She's even buying me a new mining pick! Thinking about how we'll be able to use the same pick to mine together makes me feel our bond growing even closer.

He had finally managed to enter this mine, intending to save up enough Spirit Stones to advance his cultivation. After months of hard work, it seemed all his efforts had amounted to nothing. Yet, whenever he thought of Sister Yinyin's smiles and glances, he felt that finding such a cultivation partner made it all worthwhile!
With that resolved, Senior Brother Song chipped the spirit ore free from the rock and handed it to Lin Yinyin.
"I'm off to exchange this for Spirit Stones now, Senior Brother. Please wait for me!"

As he watched Lin Yinyin skip away, Senior Brother Song felt as though her delicate fragrance still lingered in the air. Yet, when he turned back to look at the now-empty mining pit, a faint pang of regret tugged at his heart.
At the Spirit Ore Refining Station.
One of the supervisors on duty was Zhao Jia.
Foundation Establishment, Third Level. Male. No cultivation partner.

He took great pride in his position. This mine was renowned throughout the surrounding hundred li. In the cultivation world, only those who paid the fee—or pulled strings through connections—were allowed to enter and mine.
The reason was simple: mining was incredibly profitable!
Anyone entering this mine had to turn over all their output to the refining station. The mine took eighty percent of the yield, leaving the remaining twenty percent for the miners.

Normally, a miner could produce around a hundred low-grade Spirit Stones per month, netting twenty after the cut. With extra effort or luck, even more was possible. Typically, an ordinary Qi Refining cultivator around the Shuiyun Sect earned less than ten low-grade stones per month. That was why so many people were eager to squeeze their way into this mine.
And Zhao Jia himself, so young yet already holding the position of Refining Supervisor, naturally enjoyed an exalted status.
The main reason, of course, was his grandfather—who owned this very spirit vein.
As a rich third-generation heir, he didn't really need to be on duty every day. But recently...
"Yinyin, you're here to refine ore again!" He spotted the pale yellow figure from afar and waved, flashing what he thought was a handsome, warm smile.
"Mn!" Lin Yinyin stepped forward, took out her spirit ore, and exhaled softly. "It's Supervisor Zhao Jia again today—what a coincidence!"
She casually brushed her hair aside with practiced ease.

Zhao Jia took the spirit ore, deftly tossed it into the Spirit Furnace behind him, and pretended to inspect the ore while actually admiring Lin Yinyin. "The quality is quite good. You work so hard mining every day, yet your skin remains so fair. Clearly, you're doing well with your Water Spirit Art practice!"

"I just want to support myself!" Lin Yinyin stuck out her tongue, then playfully flipped up the hem of her short skirt, inadvertently revealing a glimpse of her rounded thigh. "My legs are actually quite tan!"
Ha! The Water Spirit Art couldn't possibly make one's skin this fair. Her mother spent five low-grade Spirit Stones each month buying Spirit Pearls ground into powder for skincare!
Zhao Jia glanced at her thigh, feeling a sudden heat rise within him—a pure yet subtly sensual sensation that was almost too much to bear.
After a short chat, the furnace finished refining. Zhao Jia said, "This ore is excellent—it yielded fifty-eight Spirit Stones. Here are fifteen for you."
"Ah! Senior Brother Zhao, did you miscalculate? There are Surveillance Arrays here!"
"It doesn't matter. This vein belongs to my family. I still have some authority."
"Haha! Thank you, Elder Brother Zhao Jia!"

Watching Lin Yinyin walk away, Zhao Jia secretly rejoiced. Although his previous attempt to invite Sister Yinyin to his grandfather's birthday banquet had been rejected, this time she had agreed to accompany him to an auction!
Perfect timing to introduce her to the wider world. Sister Yinyin is wonderful in every way—except for her stubborn insistence on supporting herself rather than letting me take care of her.
Lin Yinyin, however, had her own worries.

Senior Brother Zhao's advances have become too intense lately. I need to find a way to cool things down. It's a pity, though—his family background is quite impressive. If only his grandfather didn't have over a hundred other grandchildren, I might have seriously considered it.
As Lin Yinyin pondered these thoughts, she arrived at an open space nearby where dozens of stalls were scattered. Due to the spirit vein, the area had gradually developed into a small trading market.
"Spirit Stone Exchange - At a Loss"
An unassuming little stall caught Lin Yinyin's attention. The cultivator sitting quietly behind it looked somewhat simple and honest—a middle-aged man.
Lin Yinyin had heard of him. His name was Zhang Xian.

He had arrived about a week ago, reportedly paying a considerable sum of low-grade Spirit Stones to gain entry through connections. Strangely, he hadn't started mining at all. Instead, he'd set up this stall to trade Spirit Stones.

Logically speaking, the exchange rate for Spirit Stones of different attributes was usually fixed at one-to-one, with little fluctuation. Occasionally, a cultivator in urgent need of a particular attribute might offer ten stones for nine.

But Zhang Xian was different. When he first opened his stall, he offered ten stones for seven, accepting only Wood-attribute stones. It was said he exchanged nearly a hundred stones that very day, losing more than twenty in the process. And now, he was doing it again.
Either he is a fool or a gullible mark. Lin Yinyin, with her keen intuition, quickly gathered all the information about this man.
Zhang Xian. Male. Qi Refining, Fifth Level. Appears simple and honest, but his bone age is over a hundred years.
A complete failure in cultivation, yet wealthy. This man has secrets!
"How do I exchange Spirit Stones?" Lin Yinyin asked softly, leaning close to the stall.
"I urgently need Wood-attribute Spirit Stones. Seven Wood stones can be exchanged here for ten generic low-grade stones."
Sure enough, here he is again. Such a lucrative deal can't be missed. Lin Yinyin counted out thirteen stones from her pouch, and the man gave her twenty.
"These are the thirteen you exchanged, and here are seven extra as a gift." The man handed over the stones. All of them were Water-attribute.
Lin Yinyin frowned slightly. This man speaks in such a strange manner!
Oh well, the Spirit Stones are already in my pocket. Hmph! How did he know I possess a Water Spirit Root? He must have noticed me long ago. Truly, this young lady is irresistibly charming.

chapters.title: Chapter 12 First, Let’s Buy the Original Flavor
paragraphs: "Young lady, please wait!" said the honest-looking cultivator. "Is the hairpin on your head for sale?"
Huh? Lin Yinyin immediately became alert.

The hairpin on her head had been bought a few years ago at a large marketplace for ten low-grade Spirit Stones. Its only function was to occasionally emit a chill, with no practical use in combat. However, its unique design was something she really loved, so she wore it often. More importantly, it was an item she kept close to her body, and she was particularly sensitive about such things.

She had just earned seven low-grade Spirit Stones from him—would it be too rude to refuse outright? Hmm... this man seems genuinely honest and kind-hearted. Could it be that he likes me and wants to collect my personal belongings?
She’d heard some people had fetishistic tendencies.
"No misunderstanding here," the honest cultivator said with clear eyes. "I have a younger sister whom I haven’t seen in many years. I want to buy her a gift."
"You’re trying to fool ghosts!" exclaimed a passerby standing nearby, nearly exposing him right then and there.

When this honest cultivator first set up his stall, this passerby had already intended to exchange Spirit Stones with him, hoping to snag a bargain. But the cultivator had flatly refused. Then, as soon as Lin Yinyin arrived, he immediately agreed to trade—clearly picking and choosing who he dealt with! And now he wanted to buy her hairpin too—obviously planning to keep it for himself!

"I’ll offer twenty low-grade Spirit Stones for your hairpin, plus I’ll give you a low-grade magical artifact called ‘Ruyi,’ which responds to your thoughts and can strike enemies from a hundred paces away."
"Most importantly, this hairpin has a lovely style—my sister would absolutely love it!"

Lin Yinyin decisively removed the hairpin and sold it. What’s more, she even received a low-grade magical artifact on top! Although both the artifact and her hairpin were of the same low-grade tier, this offensive artifact alone was worth at least thirty low-grade Spirit Stones. This transaction netted her over forty low-grade stones—a sum equivalent to her usual earnings for two months!
"You’re truly kind to your sister," Lin Yinyin said with a charming smile, deftly tucking her hair behind her ear.
Though his cultivation level is a bit low, he was certainly generous enough to enter my fishpond.

"!!" The passerby beside them was utterly stunned. "Brother, are you throwing money around too recklessly? Forty low-grade Spirit Stones could easily get you two female cultivators from the Jade Pavilion—no effort required!"
"Do you sell your spirit-cloth handkerchief too? My sister would love it as well," the cultivator continued, eager to keep buying.

Thump, thump, thump! The passerby took three staggering steps backward. Was this man really so shameless? He even wants her handkerchief for wiping sweat—is he aiming to collect her "Original Flavor"?
Lin Yinyin’s face instantly flushed red. "This handkerchief is a personal item—I can’t sell it!
A flicker of annoyance crossed her heart. Though this man was generous, he was starting to border on the bizarre. She was beginning to feel afraid.

"If you won’t sell it, how about you give it to me, and I’ll give you..." He paused, then pulled out a mid-grade Spirit Stone, its icy blue glow shimmering in his hand. "...a mid-grade Spirit Stone in return."
Lin Yinyin’s eyes widened in shock. !!
This spirit handkerchief had no other use besides absorbing sweat—it was worth only one low-grade Spirit Stone per hundred pieces.
He really is a freak! And a super-rich, money-burning freak at that!
The passerby beside them wished he could take off his own undergarments just to trade for that mid-grade Spirit Stone, roaring inwardly, Brother, your cost for courting women is way too high!

Lin Yinyin took a deep breath, lowered her lashes, and softly said, "I’m sorry, Senior Brother. Please control yourself. If you’d like to buy something for your sister, I’d be happy to accompany you another day to pick something out together."
Though a mid-grade Spirit Stone was tempting, she still had her own boundaries.
"This handkerchief is very important to me—I’ll give you ten of them." The cultivator calmly laid out ten mid-grade Spirit Stones.
The passerby beside them was completely flustered, clutching his chest as if his entire cultivation worldview had been shattered beyond recognition.
To hesitate even for half a second felt like disrespecting the Spirit Stones themselves. Lin Yinyin quickly handed over her used handkerchief and accepted the stones in return.
"Senior Brother, if there’s ever an opportunity—"
"There will be! I have urgent business to attend to, so I must take my leave now."

After handing over the handkerchief, the cultivator didn’t even look up. With a soft leap, he vanished into the mountains in the blink of an eye, leaving Lin Yinyin standing alone, disheveled in the wind.
There are still cultivators I can't figure out. All I know for sure is that this one is definitely strange—and incredibly hasty. Could he really be taking my handkerchief to do something odd?!
[Ding! Successfully gifted 7 low-grade Spirit Stones. Triggered return: 7 high-grade Spirit Stones.]
[Ding! Successfully gifted the low-grade magical artifact, Ruyi Short Sword. Triggered return: High-grade magical artifact, Yuli Sword.]
[Yuli Sword: An upper-grade magical artifact that automatically protects its owner and unsheathes itself upon sensing hostility within a hundred paces.]
[Ding! Successfully gifted 10 mid-grade Spirit Stones. Triggered return: 100 high-grade Spirit Stones.]
[Ding! Current Favorability: 1.]
The honest cultivator was overjoyed. One hundred high-grade Spirit Stones—enough for him to splurge freely!
He was none other than Zhang Xian, reborn and transformed. After spending so long in the cultivation world, Lin Yinyin was the first Daughter of Destiny he had sensed.
[Ding! Detected a Daughter of Destiny with 45 points of fortune: Lin Yinyin.]
[Ding! Lin Yinyin’s Favorability towards you is 0. Binding successful.]
When he first spotted Lin Yinyin near the mineral vein, he hadn’t acted rashly. After all, there were quite a few male cultivators surrounding her, and he didn’t want to cause unnecessary trouble.
Still—exchanging ten mid-grade Spirit Stones for a useless handkerchief was a bit too hasty.
What else could he do? He couldn’t think of a better excuse for the moment.

Zhang Xian pondered for a moment, then slipped the handkerchief into his pocket. Well, even a mosquito’s leg is meat—throwing it away would be a waste. I'm not really interested in collecting Lin Yinyin’s "Original Flavor" after all.

Zhang Xian quietly analyzed the situation. It was clear that the Daughter of Destiny’s score correlated somewhat with her cultivation level, though not significantly. As for Favorability, there wasn’t much data yet to draw conclusions. A score below zero indicated hostility. Back at the Taoist temple, Li Miaoyin’s Favorability had risen to 59 points and then plateaued, suggesting that 60 points was a critical threshold.
As for the System's returns, they always involved either upgrading an artifact’s grade or receiving tenfold the value—twice in total.

Logically speaking, upgrading the artifact’s grade was always preferable, whether it was Spirit Stones or magical artifacts. Crossing a grade level was far more advantageous than simply multiplying by ten. But he didn’t know what conditions triggered these returns, so he needed to experiment further.

The return rules were also quite restrictive. In his previous transactions, the first time he gave away seven Spirit Stones, he received a return. But the second time, when he traded a hairpin clearly worth less than twenty stones, he received no return on the stones themselves—but the accompanying dagger did trigger a return.
It seemed that only gifts given proactively could trigger a return.
Other systems offered chat interactions and alerts, but this System lacked even basic functional explanations. He had to figure everything out through trial and error, leaving him utterly exhausted.

Logically speaking, upgrading the artifact’s grade was always preferable, whether it was Spirit Stones or magical artifacts.
Crossing a grade level was far more advantageous than simply multiplying by ten.
But he didn’t know what conditions triggered these returns, so he needed to experiment further.
The return rules were also quite restrictive.
In his previous transactions, the first time he gave away seven Spirit Stones, he received a return.
But the second time, when he traded a hairpin clearly worth less than twenty stones, he received no return on the stones themselves—but the accompanying dagger did trigger a return.
It seemed that only gifts given proactively could trigger a return.
Other systems offered chat interactions and alerts, but this System lacked even basic functional explanations.
He had to figure everything out through trial and error, leaving him utterly exhausted.

chapters.title: Chapter 13 Heh heh heh, since you’ve come to me willingly...
paragraphs: Shuiyun City.
Zhang Xian effortlessly made his way back to his new residence—a cultivation estate that had cost him a full 800 mid-grade Spirit Stones.

Privacy. Seclusion. These were exactly what he sought. Though the spiritual energy here couldn’t compare to that of a sect or an immortal mountain, living within the city offered unparalleled safety. If he ventured into the remote wilderness to cultivate, he’d risk being murdered and robbed of his treasures.
As for the city’s low spiritual energy density...
Zhang Xian smoothly entered the house, tossed out five mid-grade Spirit Stones, and activated a Spirit Gathering Formation. Instantly, the spiritual energy within the room surged, thickening visibly.
He now possessed 100 high-grade Spirit Stones—equivalent to 10,000 mid-grade ones! He was indulging in nothing short of extravagant waste.
His Classic of Nurturing Golden Cores with Azure Wood had already reached the full maturity of the second stage, placing him firmly at the Fifth Level of Qi Refining.

When this scripture reached the complete maturity of its ninth stage, his False Core would also reach perfection. This was the absolute pinnacle for a rootless cultivator, currently recognized as the highest attainable level in the cultivation world. A perfected False Core roughly corresponded to the early stage of an authentic Golden Core.
But even a False Core cultivator was still an Immortal, with a lifespan approaching a thousand years. With the System by his side, everything remained possible.
Two months later. Yueyang Tower.
Today, Zhao Jia was in an exceptionally good mood. He had successfully invited Lin Yinyin out, and she had agreed to accompany him to a grand auction hosted by the Baoqing Workshop.

This auction was on an unprecedented scale. Its caliber was primarily judged by its currency: most auctions used low-grade Spirit Stones, but this one dealt exclusively in mid-grade ones—a rarity in Shuiyun City. Not only Lin Yinyin, but even Zhao Jia himself couldn’t afford a single item there. Attending was merely a chance to broaden his horizons.
In short, this auction drew elites from all walks of life, including Senior Elders from the Yunmiao Sect, one of the Southern Region’s top-tier powers.
"Heh heh! Let me show you just how wealthy the Zhao family truly is."
Zhao Jia couldn’t help but wonder if Lin Yinyin realized just how impressive he was. She often treated him with such aloofness, yet he was a wealthy third-generation heir!

He had brought her to the premier restaurant in Shuiyun City for a lavish feast, ordering their signature Spiritual Spring Wine—a bottle costing 100 low-grade Spirit Stones, a luxury even he usually begrudged himself. Surely, this would win her heart completely!
Gazing at Lin Yinyin’s slender waist, Zhao Jia felt a surge of desire. What delightful possibilities might arise if she became intoxicated?
Meanwhile, on the upper floor of the restaurant, Zhang Xian had just arrived.
"As usual, bring me the same dishes as last time."
"Right away, Honored Guest! And the Spiritual Spring Wine?"
"The usual—ten bottles. Package up whatever is left over."
"Certainly, Honored Guest!"

The servers adored patrons like Zhang Xian—tough, no-nonsense, and extravagantly generous. In recent days, with the auction taking place in Shuiyun City, many wealthy outsiders had descended upon the city. The restaurant, which normally struggled to sell even a single bottle of Spiritual Spring Wine a day, was now facing a severe shortage.
At this moment, Zhang Xian had already reached the Eighth Level of Qi Refining.

Over the past two months, his cultivation speed had skyrocketed like a rocket. The Classic of Nurturing Golden Cores with Azure Wood was an Arcane-grade cultivation technique. Coupled with his lavish cultivation method—consuming five mid-grade Spirit Stones daily, an amount equal to what ordinary cultivators earned in years—he was progressing at an astonishing pace.
[Ding! Current Favorability: 6.]
Hearing the System’s notification, Zhang Xian glanced around—and noticed Lin Yinyin seated not far away.

The Southern Region was peaceful, and every city was protected by a Star-Dou Protective Formation. This formation not only concentrated spiritual energy but also suppressed the leakage of cultivators’ spiritual power. Simply put, it rendered duels and flight impossible unless one’s internal spiritual force could overpower the formation—a feat achievable only by the most elite cultivators.
This was Zhang Xian’s primary reason for choosing to live in the city: to avoid the constant threat of being murdered for his treasures.
Seeing Lin Yinyin accompanied by a male companion, Zhang Xian decided not to disturb her.

Normally, cultivators who reached the mid-stage of Qi Refining could abstain from food altogether. Yet, human cravings were innate, especially when the ingredients used by this restaurant were rare spiritual herbs and divine birds beneficial for cultivation. Zhang Xian frequented this place often.

His behavior inevitably drew attention from other diners. Yueyang Tower wasn’t a cheap establishment; those who dined here were either conducting business meetings or enjoying romantic dates. A solitary patron like Zhang Xian, quietly devouring his meal as if it were a cafeteria lunch, was indeed unusual.
Zhao Jia couldn’t help but glance at him several times, then chuckled. "I wonder which sect this ‘Senior’ belongs to, to be so generous with his spending."
"Senior cultivator?" Lin Yinyin asked, her beautiful eyes darting repeatedly toward Zhang Xian’s figure.
She had noticed him the very moment he stepped onto the restaurant floor.

There was no helping it—the impression this "eccentric" had left on her was simply too profound. He had spent a staggering ten mid-grade Spirit Stones to purchase her used handkerchief, only to vanish for over two months.
She prided herself on her skillful use of the "leading them on" tactic, but this man’s approach was so bizarre and unpredictable that she simply couldn’t fathom it.

"That’s right. He appears to be only at the eighth level of Qi Refining, yet judging by his bone age, he must be at least a hundred years old. It wouldn’t be surprising if he were a destitute wandering cultivator. But this is Yueyang Tower! Ordering so many exquisite dishes at once—it’s beyond the means of ordinary people. I suspect he might actually be a Senior cultivator at the Golden Core stage concealing his power," Zhao Jia mused. Even his own grandfather wouldn’t dare spend so lavishly.
Techniques for concealing one’s aura were commonplace in the cultivation world. After hearing Zhao Jia’s analysis, Lin Yinyin found it rather plausible.
So this "eccentric senior" is actually at the Golden Core stage?

In the Southern Region, Qi Refining cultivators were as common as carp swimming upstream—countless in number. However, due to limitations in natural talent and resources, fewer than one in ten could break through to the Foundation Establishment stage.

The difficulty increased exponentially beyond that point. Among a hundred Foundation Establishment cultivators, not even one could advance to Golden Core. Take Shuiyun City as an example: tens of thousands of cultivators lived there, yet only a few dozen were Golden Core masters. Zhao Jia’s grandfather was one of them.

Beyond the Golden Core, each subsequent stage presented an insurmountable barrier, trapping even the most gifted. Lin Yinyin’s dream was to become a Golden Core cultivator, but beyond that, she didn’t dare to hope.
Should I go over and greet him? Lin Yinyin pondered, feeling it might seem abrupt, unbecoming of her dignified demeanor.
Yet a flicker of disappointment lingered within her. Damn it! I’m breathtakingly beautiful—how could you not notice me, after spending so much money on my handkerchief?
Lost in her thoughts, Zhang Xian continued eating, showing no sign of initiating conversation.

Across from him, Zhao Jia noticed Lin Yinyin’s distracted state. "Yinyin, what’s wrong? Is something troubling you? Drink more—this Spiritual Spring Wine isn’t just fragrant and refreshing; it’s also beneficial for cultivation, especially suited to your Water Spirit Root."
"I’m feeling a bit unwell, Brother Zhao." Lin Yinyin shook her head.
"What?" Zhao Jia’s heart skipped a beat. Why had Yinyin suddenly grown distant? Just moments ago, she had been calling him "Brother Zhao"; now she was addressing him as "Senior Brother."
Was it because I brought her here for drinks? Had she detected my intentions? Or was there some other reason?
Finally, Zhang Xian finished his meal, paid the bill, and prepared to leave.
Missing this opportunity means who knows when another will arise! To hell with dignity!
Lin Yinyin waved casually toward Zhang Xian, feigning nonchalance. "Senior Brother Zhang, what a coincidence!"
"Oh? So it’s you, Fellow Cultivator! Long time no see!" Zhang Xian greeted her with genuine surprise, bowing respectfully.
Zhao Jia leapt to his feet. "Ah! I’ve met the Senior! Yinyin, so you two know each other?"
Who is this Senior?
"I’ve met the Fellow Cultivator, but she’s mistaken—I’m no Senior." Zhang Xian politely returned the greeting.
Zhao Jia refused to believe it. After all, these old monsters loved to play coy, pretending to be weaklings before striking back with a dazzling display of power. One had to remain vigilant.
"A fleeting encounter. Senior Brother Zhang, have you met your younger sister yet?" Lin Yinyin asked with a touch of shyness.
Her delicate demeanor instantly captivated Zhao Jia—her voice soft and sweet, her cheeks flushed with a rosy hue.
Too bad it isn’t directed at me. Was this the allure of a Golden Core cultivator? He felt a pang of bitter envy.
"Yes, I have. She loves the gifts."
"Senior Brother Zhang remembers—we agreed last time to accompany you in selecting a gift."
"Perfect timing, then. I’m meeting my sister again in a few days. Let’s go now."
Heh heh heh, since you’ve come to me willingly, don’t blame me for what happens next.
"You’re truly kind to your sister. Senior Brother Zhao, I have other matters to attend to, so I’ll take my leave now."

Watching Lin Yinyin follow the "Senior" down the stairs, Zhao Jia felt a chilling autumn wind sweep through him, leaving him utterly numb. His months-long preparations for this date had been abruptly cut short—before he’d even had a chance to take off his pants.
"No!"
"My dear Yinyin! Come to your senses! I’m your true love! Don’t succumb to the Senior’s seductive power!"
